title: What Damla is for
summary: The idea in one page, and a map of the app.
text: damla is a cash-flow app that lives on your iphone. it answers one question every day: will you have enough money until your next income, and what happens if you spend, commit to something or delay something. you tell damla what happens with your money - a sentence, a form, a bank alert or a pasted message. damla keeps the books correctly: every amount moves between two places, so nothing is counted twice. all the maths - balances, instalments, forecasts, gains - is done by ordinary, tested code. the on-device model only helps read your words. your data stays on the phone: there is no account, no server and no tracking. today: the answer first, then what needs you. invented sample data. when to use it every day, to see the one number that matters: how much is safe to spend. before you buy something or commit to a payment, to see what it does to the weeks ahead. when a bank message arrives, so the transaction is recorded without typing it in. when you want to know where the money went, what you own, or whether you can afford something you have in mind. the five tabs the app has five tabs at the bottom. open damla. it asks for face id when you open it, and again only after it has been away for the length of time you choose in settings under basics, ask for face id (every time, or after 1, 5 or 15 minutes). the shortcut automations that pass bank messages to damla do not need it. today is where you land. the big teal card shows safe to spend, whether your balance stays above your minimum, and a small chart of your balance ahead (tap it for the full forecast and what if). below it you find what is coming, and anything waiting for you. tap activity to see every transaction. tap one to change it. tap accounts to see your banks, savings, cards, loans, investments, assets and people. tap insights to see where the money went, your budget, net worth and holdings. tap plan to see everything that commits future money: income and bills, instalment plans, staged purchases, bills coming, and people you lent to or owe. on today, the gear icon at the top right opens settings, where you also find the guide, your backup and the set-up guide. the book icon next to it opens the guide directly. good to know note: anything that creates a commitment (an instalment plan, a loan), or that damla is unsure about, is shown for one tap before it is written. tip: when you have no accounts yet, today shows a let's set up damla screen with a set up step by step button. the set-up guide can be reopened later from today or from settings. note: the app gives you information and estimates about your own spending. it does not give financial advice; what to spend is your decision. no account, balance, transaction or note ever leaves the phone, and the app works fully offline. the only lookups are the few optional ones, and they send no personal data - see privacy and your data . related setting up your books a day with damla forecast and safe to spend the free trial and the subscription

title: Setting up your books
summary: Your currency, your minimum balance, your accounts, income and bills, step by step.
text: set-up tells damla what it needs to give a useful answer: which currency your books are in, what you keep as a minimum, and what you own, earn and owe. do it in one sitting or in pieces. anything you skip can be done later. whatever you leave for later stays a to-do. today shows a finish setting up row until it is done. when to use it the first time you open damla, to get to your first forecast. when today shows finish setting up, to fill in something you skipped. when something changed in your life - a new card, a loan, a bill that repeats - and you want to add it in the guided way. you would rather not fill forms: every step except investments and assets also takes a plain sentence. step by step open today. if it is empty, tap set up step by step . later you can reopen the same interview from settings under set-up guide . on the first screen ( welcome to damla ) choose your main currency - the currency of your region is suggested when damla knows it. type the minimum balance to keep - the amount you want untouched. everything above it is what the app calls safe to spend. you can change the minimum later. tap start , or instead open a family snapshot (a read-only picture another user of damla sent you), or choose look around with invented numbers until you are ready to use your own figures. the next screen asks what shall we set up? , with six things you can tick: bank accounts and cash , regular income , credit cards , regular spending , loans and debts , investments and assets . tick what applies to you and tap start . you can also choose add statements instead to import pdf or csv statements. do one screen per ticked part. each has its own add button - add an account , add income , add a card , add a bill , add (a menu: a loan with instalments, or money with a person), add a holding - plus next at the bottom (or i don't have any if that part turned out to be empty) and do this later . on every screen except investments and assets you can instead type a sentence in the or just type it box and tap read it . damla reads it on the phone, fills the form and shows what it understood for you to check before anything is saved. at the end you reach all set for now : your first forecast, what it rests on, and anything you postponed as buttons you can go back to. tap go to today . what each part asks for, so you can prepare: bank accounts and cash : each bank account, savings account and cash you hold, with its balance today. regular income : salary, rent you receive, anything that arrives on a schedule, with its amount and next date. credit cards : what you owe now (split into what is already billed and what is not yet), the statement date and the payment due date (each a day of the month), and which account pays the card. regular spending : rent, school, utilities, phone, insurance, subscriptions: what leaves on a schedule. loans and debts : a loan with instalments - what is still to repay, the instalment and how many are left - or money that stands between you and a person, either you owe them or they owe you. investments and assets : shares, gold, property, a car - anything you own that has a value. you keep the values up to date yourself. tip: when a step needs an account to move the money through and you have not added one yet, the app says so and the add button waits until you do. nothing is lost by doing accounts first. good to know note: you can leave and come back at any point. progress is saved with the book. reopening from today picks up at the first step you postponed; the set-up guide row in settings starts again from the step list. tip: adding statements is optional in set-up. once your accounts exist you can import them any time to fill in history and check your numbers. note: the gaps the first forecast lists (for example no account yet, or no income set) are not errors. add the missing piece and the gap goes away. your minimum balance lives in settings under basics . change it there whenever the number you want to keep changes. related what damla is for a day with damla type a sentence the accounts page

title: A day with Damla
summary: What to look at on Today, and the small habits that keep the answer right.
text: today is the screen damla shows you every day: one big answer on top - what is safe to spend - and everything that needs you underneath. this page is the daily habit. today with the sample household. when to use it in the morning, to see what today looks like before anything leaves your account. when something is due, to record it in a tap from the due list. when a bank message went somewhere unexpected, to find it waiting for your ok. when you want to know what the money went to this month. step by step open today . the big card shows safe to spend and a verdict: either it stays above your minimum for the period, or it says you may run short before a date. tap the card to open the forecast and see day by day where the low point is. look at the three numbers under the card: balance today , the lowest point in the period with its date, and you keep , your minimum. under the numbers, anything that needs an answer appears as a row, in this order: - due (income and bills due tomorrow, today or already late, not recorded yet). - statements waiting to review (sent by the shortcut, nothing added until you confirm). - items waiting for your ok (the inbox). - bills found in your history (repeating payments damla noticed; add them in one tap). - bills coming (announced by a message but not charged yet; counted once the card is charged). - finish setting up (steps you left for later). - a backup reminder, when the automatic backup has not run for a few days, or is switched off while your books already have entries. tap the row that needs you. a due payment opens its page to record it; a card bill opens pay card bill (amount, account, date); a staged purchase opens its plan. alerts that were clear enough to record go straight into the activity list, under new from alerts . scan coming up underneath: money in and money out together, each with its date, and tappable rows that go straight to where it is recorded. if one of your bank accounts has a keep at least amount and it would dip below that before the month ends, a move … to … row appears with how much to move - tap it to see the working. read the where the money went row for how much you spent this month, and ask damla if you have a question about something you plan to do. tip: if you have set money aside for goals, a line on the teal card says how much of safe to spend is already spoken for and how much is free to spend. safe to spend itself does not change. if you see you may run short, it means the lowest point of your balance in the period falls below your minimum before the end of it. the forecast shows when. what if (a button in the forecast) lets you try spending, receiving, skipping a payment or turning something into instalments before you do it for real. good to know note: the number is only as good as the things damla knows. today's answer is worked out from your books as they are now: when you add an account, a bill or a card change, the answer is that new calculation - you never have to refresh anything yourself. limit: everyday spending that is not a bill and comes from your bank accounts is not taken out of the balance day by day in the forecast. that is what your minimum is for: keep a cushion, not an exact figure, for the ordinary days. note: in the last three days of the free trial a one-line banner about the trial appears near the top of today, with a subscribe button. today's answer always comes first. small habits that keep the answer right: record things when they happen - type a sentence in the add menu, or let your bank messages reach damla through a shortcut so it happens by itself. open the inbox and clear what is waiting for your ok, rather than leaving it. when something repeats that is not a bill yet, add it from the bills found in your history row so the forecast counts it. keep the backup reminder clear: everything lives on the phone, so the backup is your copy. when the answer says short, look early: open the forecast. related setting up your books forecast and safe to spend what if backup and restore

title: The free trial and the subscription
summary: 45 days free, then one subscription with every feature; what read-only means.
text: damla is free for 45 days, then one subscription - damla core, monthly or yearly - keeps everything open. there are no feature tiers: the subscription unlocks editing, or the app is read-only. you can start and use the trial without entering any payment details. when to use it when you first wonder what damla costs and what happens when the trial ends. when you saw a card about the trial on today and want to know what it means. if the trial has ended and you want to know what you can still do. when the subscription is running and you want to check, restore or manage it. what the trial is the 45 days start when you set up your first book in damla, not when you install the app. the trial is tracked on the phone. you are never asked for payment details during it, because it is not the app store's introductory offer. it does not restart if you reinstall the app or delete your data. a copy of the trial record survives both, so the clock keeps running from where it is. during the trial, everything works: adding, changing, forecasts, what if, insights. in the last three days of the trial, today shows a one-line banner with the days left and a subscribe button. how to subscribe open settings, then subscription , and tap the row to open the damla core screen (the same screen the subscribe buttons on today open). your current state appears first: how many free days are left, or which plan you have and when it renews. choose monthly or yearly . the price shown is the localized price from the app store. if prices have not loaded, nothing is shown instead. tap subscribe . payment is charged to your apple id, and the subscription renews automatically until you cancel it in settings on your iphone under your name, subscriptions. if you subscribe while the trial is still running, your plan starts today. the remaining free days are not added to it. lower on the same screen are two more buttons. restore purchases brings back a subscription you already bought on this apple id if it did not arrive. manage subscription opens apple's own subscription page and appears only when you have a subscription. after the trial ends today shows a card saying the trial has ended and that damla is read-only for now, with a subscribe button to open the plans. in read-only you can still open every screen: read your transactions, accounts and charts, use the forecast, export your data to a spreadsheet, back it up, restore a backup, and delete your data. settings, this guide and restore purchases all stay open. what stops is adding and changing: new transactions, new accounts, new plans for the future, and edits. when an edit stops, an explanation appears once at the bottom of the screen - never as an error box - with two choices, subscribe and not now (when the reason is a failed renewal, only not now ). nothing deletes your data when the trial or subscription ends. subscribing again unlocks the same books exactly where you left them. note: check the price on the damla core screen at the moment of purchase before you tap subscribe. good to know note: once, during the trial, a card may appear on today after damla has done something for you - it says what (for example how many transactions were added from your bank messages by themselves, or a bill matched to the charge that paid it). it does not move the end of the trial and can be dismissed with not now . limit: the trial clock is measured in days and never resets, so an app store reinstall does not earn new days. the remaining time comes from two copies of the record: one in the keychain, and one in damla's own store that travels with a backup. note: when a renewal fails, apple's billing grace period keeps damla working while apple retries the payment, and the app tells you to update your payment method. if the retries run out, damla goes read-only until the payment succeeds; then it picks up where it left off. related what damla is for export and the family snapshot backup and restore privacy and your data

title: Type a sentence
summary: Say what happened in your own words and Damla fills the form.
text: type what happened - "lunch 45 at zuma from visa" - and damla reads it into an amount, an account, a category and a date. you check what it found and confirm with one tap. nothing is saved until you do. it is a form that fills itself in from your own words. if damla reads something wrong or misses a part, you finish the rest in the normal form, starting from what it understood. type a sentence and damla fills the form. when to use it when you just paid for something or received money, and you want to record it without filling a form. when you got a bank message or an email about money that damla did not catch automatically: paste it in. when you want to turn a card purchase into instalments by saying so, for example "school payment on the everyday card, now 6 months". when you want to note a bill: a message that a bill is ready or due, with its amount or a due date, is remembered as a bill coming. step by step tap the plus button on today or activity. tap type a sentence . the add by sentence screen opens with the keyboard ready. write what happened in your own words, with the amount, an account or card name, and a date if it was not today. the example shown in the field is "for example: lunch 45 at zuma from visa". you can also write a commitment, such as putting a purchase on instalments. tap continue . the button shows reading… while damla reads the words, then the section called check and save shows what it found. if everything is right, tap save . if a part is missing or unclear, damla says what it needs and offers complete it , which opens the form with what was understood already filled in. finish it there and save. two shortcuts: paste puts the clipboard in the field and reads it straight away, without another tap. this is for bank texts or emails you copied. a message that arrives from your shortcut, the share sheet or the inbox opens this same screen already read: the first thing you see is the check and save section. what you can see in check and save an ordinary payment or income: the amount, the accounts it moves between, the payee and the date. tap save. something that looks already recorded: the section warns "this looks like something already recorded." and offers save anyway. check it first - paying twice is possible. a purchase turned into instalments: the reading shows the instalment, the number of months, the first date and any fee, with the note "this creates a commitment, so please check it." the button is create plan . it stays a suggestion until you tap it. something incomplete: "i need a bit more:" lists the questions, such as "how much?" or "which account does it come from?", and complete it opens the form. a bill notice: "this is a bill notice." damla remembers it as an expected bill. the card charge that later pays it is the one real transaction, so nothing is counted twice. a card statement notice: "this is a card statement notice." tap review the statement to go through it. if the sentence is a bank alert with the amounts printed in the usual shape, code reads it. only sentences that do not look like an alert go through the sentence reader. good to know note: where the iphone supports apple intelligence, the on-device model reads your words - nothing is sent anywhere. every amount, name and date the model returns must appear in your sentence or it is ignored, so a number it got wrong cannot creep in silently. the account and category names it returns must match your real accounts, or your own words for them are kept instead. limit: if apple intelligence is not available on your phone, damla uses a simpler on-device reader. the screen says so and asks you to check the result before saving; missing parts open the form with complete it . limit: damla reads better when you use the names you actually use for accounts. if it cannot tell which account you meant, it asks, rather than guessing. note: no transaction or plan is written to your books until you tap save, save anyway or create plan. anything that creates a commitment, or that damla is unsure about, is always shown for one tap first. after you save, damla remembers how you categorised the payee, so the next message from the same shop is filed in that category on its own. related fill a form paste or share a message the inbox instalment plans

title: Fill a form
summary: Record an expense, income or transfer with the form.
text: the form records one thing that happened: money spent, money received, a move between your own accounts, or a card bill paid from a bank account. use it when you want to check every field yourself, or to finish something damla read but could not complete on its own. the entry form. when to use it you want to record something by hand, field by field. damla read a sentence or a message but something was missing: complete it opens this form with what was understood already filled in. an item from the inbox needs completing. you want to change or correct something you recorded earlier. step by step tap the plus button on today or activity. tap fill a form . the new entry screen opens. at the top, pick the kind. the four kinds are spent , received , moved and paid card . type the amount and set the date. choose the accounts, and a category for spending or income: - spent : choose paid from - a bank, savings, wallet or card account - and a category. - received : choose a category and the account the money goes into . - moved : choose from and to . the list holds your bank, savings and wallet accounts and people. they cannot be the same account. - paid card : choose paid from - a bank, savings or wallet account - and the card . for spent or received you can add who you paid or who paid you ("paid to (optional)" or "from whom (optional)") and a note. tap save . note: moving money or paying a card is never counted as spending. a move only changes where the money sits; paying a card pays its bill. if it was in another currency for spent or received , once you have chosen the account, the form shows a paid in another currency section. if the merchant charged a currency other than the account's, pick it under charged in and type the amount charged . damla then offers use the estimate: … - the amount worked out from the latest exchange rate and the bank's markup (set in settings). a figure you type yourself replaces the estimate. if there is no exchange rate for that currency yet, type what the card was billed: it is on the statement or in the bank app. for moved between two accounts in different currencies, a received section appears: type the amount received in the receiving account's currency. changing something you recorded open activity and tap the transaction. the same form opens, titled edit entry. (a transaction that is already split opens the split sheet instead.) change what you need and tap save . to remove it, swipe the transaction in the activity list to delete it. after you save a transaction with a category, damla remembers that the shop or person belongs there, so the next alert from them is filed in that category on its own. if earlier transactions from the same shop are in a different category, damla asks whether to change them too: change them to … or only this one . the fallback category other is not remembered. good to know changing the kind after you have picked accounts clears them, so pick the kind first. under the category picker, tap new category… to create one on the spot; it is selected right away. the new-category sheet suggests an icon from the name - gym, pets, kids, insurance, repairs and many more have one built in - and lets you pick your own from a grid. the icon shows in activity. the same sheet opens from settings, categories, where you can also rename or remove categories later. if you are completing a bank alert about a card or account damla did not know yet, picking the account in the form teaches it those last digits: the next alert from it needs no question. an amount that was only estimated from a rate is kept as an estimate; the statement replaces it with the amount the bank really billed. type the real figure when you know it. tip: to share one payment among several categories (a supermarket shop that was groceries and school supplies), swipe it right in activity and tap split . to enter something you buy again and again, swipe it right and tap duplicate : a new form opens with the same amount, account, category and payee, dated today, and nothing is saved until you tap save . moves between accounts, card payments and split transactions cannot be duplicated. related type a sentence the inbox the activity list credit cards

title: Paste or share a message
summary: Send a bank text or email to Damla by pasting it or with the share sheet.
text: when a bank message did not reach damla by itself, you can hand it over: copy the text and paste it into add by sentence, or share it from messages with the share sheet. sharing behaves like the automatic alert: clear payments are added at once, anything unclear waits in the inbox. pasting shows you what damla found first, and you confirm before anything is saved. when to use it a bank text or email arrived and no automation caught it. you have not set up the shortcut for that bank yet. you want to see what damla makes of a message before anything is saved. set up the share sheet (once) open the shortcuts app, tap the plus button and add the action add to damla . in its text field, tap the shortcut input suggestion above the keyboard so it appears as a blue pill. if you type the words "shortcut input" yourself, they are sent as plain text and nothing works. tap the info button and turn on show in share sheet , accepting text. name it damla . after that, when you share text, damla appears under shortcuts. paste a message copy the message text. tap the plus button on today or activity, then type a sentence . tap paste . the text goes into the field and is read straight away. read what damla found under check and save, then tap save . if something is missing, tap complete it and finish in the form. share a message in messages, select the bank message text and tap share. tap damla under shortcuts. the shortcut runs the same reading as the automation: a clear payment is added at once, and anything unclear waits in the inbox for one tap. what damla does with the message when you paste, the result is shown on the app screen, and nothing is saved until you confirm: a clear purchase, refund or income, where the card or account digits match one of your accounts: it is shown under check and save for one tap. something that would create a commitment, such as putting a purchase on instalments: the plan is shown and needs create plan . a card statement notice: damla asks you to review the statement . something unclear: the screen says what is missing and offers complete it to finish it in the form. something that looks already recorded: the screen says "this looks like something already recorded." and offers save anyway . check it first - paying twice is possible. on both paths: a bill notice ("your bill is ready"): not a transaction - it is remembered as an expected bill, and the charge that later pays it is the one real transaction. when you share through the shortcut, an unclear message - or one that commits future money - waits in the inbox for one tap (see the inbox). note: if the message is a bank alert in the usual shape, code reads it. anything else goes through the sentence reader: where the iphone supports apple intelligence, the on-device model reads the words and nothing is sent anywhere, and every amount, name and date it returns must appear in your text or it is ignored. where it is not available, damla uses a simpler reader and asks you to check the result before saving. after you save a bank message that printed the balance afterwards, damla compares it with its books. if they disagree, the screen says "saved. one more thing" and offers match the bank's balance - a correction that is not income or spending - or leave it . good to know tip: paste and share handle one message at a time. to catch messages as they arrive, set up the shortcut (see bank texts and emails). related type a sentence the inbox bank texts and emails how automatic capture works

title: The inbox
summary: Where anything unclear waits for one tap from you.
text: the inbox holds bank messages damla did not act on by itself - because they were unclear, or because acting would commit future money. nothing from the inbox enters your books until you tap; each item is a short review. the inbox: anything unclear waits here for one tap. when to use it today shows n waiting for your ok . a payment you expected has not appeared in activity. an alert mentioned a card or account damla does not know yet. step by step open today and tap n waiting for your ok . tap an item. it opens in the normal add screen with the message already read. check what damla found under check and save. if something is missing, tap complete it and fill the rest in the form. tap save . the item leaves the inbox once you save it. to discard an item instead, tap it and then discard . to remove several at once, tap edit in the list and delete them. a statement notice does not offer you a transaction to save: tap review the statement to open the statement review. apply it and it leaves the inbox. why a message is waiting an instalment plan: it commits future money, so it needs your ok. a card payment: the message does not say which account paid it. digits that match no account yet: complete it once and damla learns those digits for good. a purchase in a currency damla has no exchange rate for yet: it asks what the card was billed. a possible duplicate of a payment added a moment ago: discard it if it is the same purchase. a message that could not be read as a bank alert at all. a statement notice, which is about the card's bill, not a purchase. good to know note: anything that creates a commitment (an instalment plan, a loan) or that damla is unsure about is always shown for one tap before it is saved. clear purchases, refunds and income whose card or account digits match one of your accounts are added at once and never see the inbox. the same message delivered twice - a shortcut that fired twice, a forwarded copy - waits once, not twice. a one-time code is dropped and never kept. a message that is not about money at all is not kept and not listed, so a private message never lands in the inbox. an alert that arrives while the phone is locked waits on the phone and is added the next time you open and unlock the app. a transaction you save from the inbox is kept as having come from a bank alert, so it shows in activity like any other alert-added one. recent alerts recent alerts, in settings, is a log of the last 50 alerts, newest first. each has a short reason: added, waiting in the inbox (and why), already recorded, ignored, or noted (a bill coming). use it to check that your automation runs, and to see why a message went where it did. related paste or share a message how automatic capture works what damla ignores, and undoing an alert credit cards

title: The Activity list
summary: Everything that happened, filters, search, undo, duplicate, split.
text: activity lists every transaction damla has recorded, grouped by day with the newest day first. it is where you check what happened, find a payment again, and change, delete, duplicate or split an entry. activity: everything that happened. when to use it to see what came in and went out on a day, and what the day came to. to catch up on what automatic bank alerts added since you last looked. to find a payment by name, note or account. to correct, remove, repeat or split a transaction after it is recorded. step by step open the activity tab. the list shows every day damla knows about, newest first. to add something, tap the add menu (the plus button) and choose type a sentence or fill a form . to narrow the list, tap filter . in the show part choose one kind only: everything, from alerts, spending, income, transfers, adjustments or starting balances. in the same menu, under account, pick one account or all accounts. to find something, type in the search box above the list. it matches what you typed against payees, notes and account names. tap a transaction to change it. a normal entry opens in the form; an entry split across categories opens the split sheet. swipe a transaction left and tap delete to remove it. on a row in the day list, swipe right (from the left edge) to see the other actions: duplicate (for a spending or an income), turn into instalments (for card purchases) and split . you can also press and hold a spending or an income for its duplicate action. to see the full list again, adjust the filter or clear the search box. good to know note: the section called new from alerts sits on top of the list, showing what automatic alerts added since you last looked, each row with a new mark. the small icon on each of those rows says where it came from: a text message, an email or a wallet payment. it shows filled and in colour while it is new, then grey. those rows offer only delete by swiping; the other actions appear on the rows in the day list. the number at the right of each day heading is the day's total: money in less money out. moves between your own accounts and card payments are not counted in it, and a day with only those shows no total at all. money out is shown with a minus, money in with a plus in green. moves between your own accounts and adjustments are grey. a purchase in another currency that is still an estimate shows its amount with an ≈ sign until the statement confirms it. starting balances are not events, so they are kept out of the plain list. to see them, use filter > starting balances, or search. duplicate opens a new form with the same amount, account, category and payee, dated today. nothing is saved until you tap save in that form. moves between accounts, card payments and split transactions cannot be duplicated. split is for one payment that covers several categories, such as a supermarket shop that was groceries and one school thing. choose a category and an amount for each part until nothing is left to share. the payment itself does not change; a transaction that is already split opens the same sheet when you tap it. turn into instalments appears only for a card purchase that is not already on an instalment plan. it opens the instalment form, where you type the numbers your bank states — the monthly instalment, the number of months, any fee and the first date — and tap convert . nothing changes until you do. limit: deleting is immediate from the swipe: the removed entry leaves the list at once, with no confirmation step. check the row is the right one before you swipe; when you remove a spending or an income, the day's figure changes with it. related type a sentence fill a form the inbox starting balances and adjustments

title: The Accounts page
summary: Your banks, savings, wallets, cards, loans and people in one list.
text: accounts lists everything that holds or owes money, grouped into sections you can collapse. it is the page for your whole position: what you could spend, what the cards owe, and where each account stands. accounts: cash, savings, cards and loans. when to use it to see your cash at a glance, and how much of it sits in savings versus what cards owe. to open one account and read the numbers that matter for its type. to add a new account or a person, or bring in a statement or screenshots. to rename an account, change its logo, include or exclude it from the forecast, or archive it. step by step open the accounts tab. the top card, cash in your accounts , adds up bank accounts, savings and wallets in your main currency; card debt is not taken off it. below the figure are owed on cards and, when your savings are not zero, of it in savings . scroll to the sections. each one — bank accounts, savings, cash and wallets, credit cards, loans, investments, assets, people — shows how many accounts it holds and, when a single total can be worked out in one currency, that total. sections you do not use do not appear. tap a section's header to collapse or open it. tap a row to open it. banks, savings, wallets, cards and loans open as a card. investments open the holding's page, assets open the staged purchase, people open the person. tap the big card to flip it. the front shows the balance (or you owe for cards and loans) and the figures for its type. the back shows more, plus its last few movements. on the back of the card, tap spending to see where its money went, transactions for everything with running balances, or details to change the account. to add something, tap the plus button and choose add an account , add a person , import statements or update from screenshots . good to know note: today's balance today counts only the accounts that take part in the forecast. the top card's of it in savings line is there to show how much of the total is savings. the back of each card carries the numbers for its type: for a card its statement and due dates and the next bill, for a loan the instalment, how often, how many are left and who pays it, for a bank its lowest point in the forecast and recent movement. in details you can rename the account, choose its logo, include or exclude it from the forecast, and archive the account after a confirmation. for anything other than a card or a loan you can also set a minimum balance to keep. for a card you set its billing cycle. an archived account keeps its history but disappears from forms and the forecast. a section's total shows only when one currency covers it — for money accounts, when every account in it uses the same currency; for investments, when their value can be worked out. a warning on the top card, n accounts left out: no exchange rate , tells you when an account in another currency could not be converted. for an account in another currency, the account form asks you for an exchange rate once, when no rate is known yet. on the day you enter a rate, yours wins; a newer fetched rate replaces it at the next refresh. tip: you do not have to finish everything here in one go. add the accounts you pay from first; investments, assets and people can wait. related credit cards loans logos and account details starting balances and adjustments

title: Credit cards
summary: Statements, due dates, what you owe now and what the next bill will be.
text: damla records a card purchase on the day it happens, and the cash leaves your bank on the day you pay the bill. you see both where the money goes and when it goes. a credit card: what you owe and the next bill. when to use it to add a card and set its billing cycle. to see what you owe now, what the next bill will be and when it is due. to tell damla what your last statement says is still unpaid. to spread a large purchase over instalments. step by step add the card: on accounts tap the plus button and choose add an account , pick the card type and enter what you owe today. open the card from accounts, tap the card to flip it and tap details . under billing cycle , choose paid from — the bank account, savings or wallet that pays the bill. without a paying account, the forecast cannot see the card bill. set statement date and payment due date with the steppers, each as a day of the month. the footer shows the next statement and payment dates so you can check them against your bank's app. once damla has a last statement to show, details gains a last statement section. enter the amount your bank says is still unpaid in still to pay and tap update the last statement . damla then pays that on its due date, and the rest of what you owe comes with the next statement. enter 0 once you have paid it. optionally, fill in typical month of spending : what the card usually spends in a statement. the forecast uses it for statements that have not been issued yet. good to know note: a card purchase is an expense on the day it happens, with a category, and feeds your spending reports. paying the statement is a transfer from your bank to the card, so the money is not counted as spending a second time. the forecast takes the cash out of your bank account on the card's due date, not on the purchase date. the card opens in accounts saying you owe . when damla can see a bill coming, the card shows the next bill and its date; until then it shows what you spent in the last 30 days. the back of the card shows the statement date and due date with the next date of each, the next bill with its amount, the account it is paid from and what was spent in the last 30 days. the still to pay figure matters. without it, everything you owe counts as the next statement, a month away. with it, the total you owe does not change — only when it will leave. typical month of spending is a starting figure only. a statement that has been issued always keeps its real amount, and once the card has as many complete months in damla as the expected card spending setting averages, the average of those months replaces it. leave it empty to use the card's own history from the start. that history needs two complete months; until then, the amount of the last statement is used. you can also enter the still to pay amount when you add the card. once damla knows the card's last digits, bank alerts add their purchases by themselves. an alert whose digits match no account yet waits in the inbox; complete it once and damla learns the digits. to spread a purchase over months, swipe it in activity and tap turn into instalments , or say so in a sentence. type the numbers from your bank's offer — the instalment, the months, any fee — and tap convert . with a sentence, damla shows the plan it read before creating it. nothing changes until you tap the button. damla does not work out interest. note: a purchase in another currency is recorded in the card's own currency as an estimate, worked out from the latest exchange rate and the markup you set under settings, card purchases in another currency (2.5% when you leave it empty). it shows with an ≈ mark and the amount the merchant charged. when the statement is imported, the estimate is replaced by what the bank really billed. if damla has no rate for that currency yet, the alert waits in the inbox and asks what the card was billed; it is never guessed. related the accounts page instalment plans importing a statement forecast and safe to spend

title: Loans
summary: Track a loan, its instalments and what is left to repay.
text: a loan in damla is the money you still owe, kept as its own account, together with the instalments that pay it off. the instalments go into your forecast until the last one, so your safe-to-spend figure already allows for them. a loan card. when to use it you are paying off a loan in instalments — a car loan, a personal loan, a student loan — and want the payments counted in your forecast until the loan is finished. you want to see in one place the instalment amount, how often it falls, how many payments are left and what is still owed. you want to record each instalment as you pay it, including the part that is interest. you want to check a loan's balance against what your bank says you owe. step by step add a loan open settings, then set-up guide. tick loans and debts, and tap start . on the step, tap add , then a loan with instalments . you can also type a sentence in the box under or just type it instead of filling the form. either way, damla shows you the loan before anything is saved. enter the details: who lent it, in lender (for example the bank) ; the amount still to repay, in still to repay ; the amount of the instalment ; how often it falls — every month, every 2 months, or any every-n days, weeks, months or years; how many instalments are left, in instalments left ; the date of the next instalment ; and the account that pays, in paid from . tap save . open accounts and check that the loan is listed under loans, as money you owe. the instalments are in your forecast from then on, until the last one, and then they stop. record an instalment open the loan from accounts and tap the card to flip it. tap details . under record an instalment , choose the account the instalment was paid from ( paid from ). enter the amount paid and, if your bank states it, how much of it was interest ( of which interest (optional) ). check the date in paid on — it can be today or earlier — then tap record the instalment . the loan goes down by the part that is not interest. the interest is booked as a cost, under fees & interest. damla does not calculate interest; it uses the numbers from your bank. good to know the back of the loan card shows what matters for this kind of account: the instalment, how often it falls, how many instalments are left, the next instalment, the date of the last one (when the loan ends), the account that pays it and what is still owed. if no instalment plan is set up for the loan, the card says so. use the set-up guide for a loan you are actively paying off. adding a loan from accounts with the plus button, then add an account , then a type of loan , records only the debt itself. without an instalment, it is not in your forecast. a loan you take out to buy a car or a property is created together with the purchase (see property and cars). a loan instalment you mark paid from today or from plan pays the loan down. it is not counted as spending. over time a loan balance can drift from your bank's figure. correct it to the balance your bank shows now and then. the correction shows as an adjustment, which is neither income nor spending. the loans section on the accounts page shows how many loans you have, and their total when they share a currency. in the loan's details you can also rename it, change its logo, include or exclude it from the forecast, and archive it. archiving keeps the loan's history; it disappears from forms and the forecast. note: a loan counts as money you owe, so it is part of what you owe in your net worth, which lives in insights. related the accounts page income and bills that repeat property and cars forecast and safe to spend

title: People: lent and borrowed
summary: Money you lent or owe, person by person.
text: people keeps a balance with each person you lend money to or borrow from. lending is not spending and being repaid is not income: the money moves between your account and the person, so your spending and income figures are not affected. people: money lent and borrowed. when to use it you lent someone money and want to remember who owes whom, and how much. you borrowed from a family member or a friend and want to see what you still owe. you want repayments kept out of your spending and income figures, while the money still moves in and out of your accounts. step by step open plan, then people: lent and borrowed, and tap add . type the person's name in the box headed new person and tap add . open the person from the list. under record , choose what happened: i lent , i borrowed , they paid me back or i paid them back . enter the amount, the account the money moved through and the date, then tap save . the person's balance shows who owes whom: positive means they owe you, negative means you owe them. when nothing is owed either way, it says all settled . good to know you can also add a person from accounts: tap the plus button, then add a person . people also appear on the accounts page, under people, each with who owes whom and by how much. lending or being repaid is never counted as spending or income. the money moves between your account and the person, and nowhere else. a person can have a balance in more than one currency. each balance is kept in its own currency; the list shows a line for each. to add a debt that already exists when you start, use the set-up guide. in the loans and debts step, tap add , then money with a person . if a balance will not be repaid, open the person and use the button at the bottom of the page: write off money owed to you that will not be repaid, or mark what you owe as forgiven. a repayment you record moves real money on the day you enter it. it is in your account balances from that day, and the forecast starts from those balances. note: the people list is sorted by name, and each row shows the balance at a glance. at the top of a person's page the balance is written out in full — sam owes you , or you owe sam . careful: this page is for money between people. a loan from a bank, paid back in instalments, belongs under loans instead. related loans the accounts page setting up your books forecast and safe to spend

title: Logos and account details
summary: Name an account, pick a logo, set the digits Damla uses to recognise it.
text: every account in damla has a name and a badge — its bank's logo, or a colour with the first letters of its name. it can also carry the last digits of its account or card number. the name and the badge are for you, so you recognise the account at a glance. the digits are for damla: they tell it which account a bank message is about. the account form. when to use it you are adding an account and want to give it a name and its bank's logo. a bank alert waits in the inbox because damla does not yet know the card's or account's digits. you want to rename an account later, keep a minimum balance in it, leave it out of the forecast, or archive it. step by step name an account and choose a logo while adding an account (accounts, plus button, add an account ), type a name in name (for example the bank) . tap the logo row. the logo screen offers no logo (initials) — a colour badge with the account's first letters — a list of banks under banks , and a search under not in the list? . tap a bank in the list to use it. if the bank is not in the list, type its name in the bank name field and tap find logo online . tap the result you want. damla downloads it and keeps it on this phone. tap cancel to leave the logo as it was. the bank name field starts as the account's name, but you can change it. for example, an account called maas at a bank can be searched by the bank's name instead. once what you type is different from the account's name, the built-in list narrows to matching banks. if nothing matches, the whole list comes back. save the digits damla should match when you add the account, type them in last digits in bank alerts (optional) : the last 4 to 6 digits of the account or card number, as your bank prints them in its messages and emails. to add them later — or to add another number — open the account, tap the card to flip it, and tap details . under numbers in bank alerts , type the digits in the field and tap add (the plus sign). swipe a saved number to remove it. tap save . good to know the digits tell damla which account an alert is about. the last 4 or 6 digits is enough; if your bank prints 4 digits and you saved 6, they still match. damla accepts 4 to 8 digits, and the same digits cannot be saved on two accounts. the first alert from each card or account goes to the inbox, because damla does not know its last digits yet. complete it once and damla remembers the digits for good. you can take them away again in the account's details. find logo online runs only when you tap it. it sends only the bank name you typed, as a logo search, to wikimedia commons. no amounts and no other details are sent. the logo you confirm is cached on this phone. before the name is sent, words that describe the account rather than the bank — savings, current, card and the like — are dropped from it. damla may try up to three search phrasings, one after another, and stops at the first that finds something. logos belong to their banks and are for your own use. the logo row is also on the account's details screen, so you can change a logo at any time. other settings live on the same details screen: keep at least , a minimum balance damla warns you about (not shown for cards and loans); include in forecast ; and archive account . archiving keeps the account's history, and it disappears from forms and the forecast. the logo appears on the account's row and on its card in accounts. note: the logo search is the only part of naming an account that touches the internet, and it happens only on your tap. everything else here is kept on the phone. related the accounts page bank texts and emails the inbox privacy and your data

title: Starting balances and adjustments
summary: How an account's opening figure works and how to correct it.
text: a starting balance is the figure you enter for an account when you bring its books into damla. it says where the account stood when you began, so nothing before that day has to be entered. an adjustment is an entry damla writes to make your books agree with what your bank or a statement says. both show as grey rows in activity, with no plus or minus sign: they are neither income nor spending, so they never change what your reports say you earned or spent. when to use it you add a bank account, savings, wallet, card or loan and enter its balance today. if that figure is not zero, damla records it as the account's starting balance. you import a statement and not all of the money was captured transaction by transaction — a card you started tracking mid-cycle, or a missed bank alert. damla books the difference as an adjustment. a number in your books does not match your bank's app, and you want to bring it into line. you want to see the corrections damla has made to its books. step by step open activity, the list of every transaction. tap filter and choose starting balances to see the opening figures, or adjustments to see the rows damla wrote: its corrections, with the opening figures among them. read a starting-balance row: it is named after the account, and the short line under it says starting balance . where damla corrected what a holding cost, the row says cost corrected and names the holding instead. read an adjustment row: it is titled adjustment , and the short line under it names the account and the reason damla wrote. to bring an account into line, the fix is always an entry, never a figure you retype. update the account with update from screenshots using your bank app, or import a statement and let damla reconcile. there is no field that overwrites the balance of an account you already use; damla writes the correcting entry for you. note: every amount in damla's books moves between two places. a starting balance or adjustment takes the difference from one reserved account named opening balances . that is why it can sit outside spending and income without anything being counted twice. good to know why starting balances are hidden starting balances are hidden from the plain activity list, because they are part of set-up and not something that happened. searching, or choosing one account in the same filter menu, shows them again. adjustments have plain-word reasons an adjustment's short line names the account and the reason, for example "balance brought forward" or "up to the statement". damla stores each reason with the reserved opening "reconciliation: " and leaves that opening off in the list. the entry is also marked as written by an import, so damla can recognise its own adjustments later. adjustments written by older versions of the app, which used the same words without the opening, are recognised too. a statement import tidies up the adjustments in its period when you import a statement that states a closing balance, damla reconciles the account: earlier adjustments inside the statement's period are removed. at most two fresh ones are added: one so the books before the period equal the statement's opening balance, and one for anything still missing at the end. afterwards your books match the statement's opening and closing balances, and every transaction counts once. if a statement does not state a closing balance, nothing is reconciled: without that figure there is nothing to reconcile to. if every row of the statement is already recorded, the import button reads reconcile to the statement , and the same tidy-up still runs. note: a card owes money in two parts: the statement your bank has already issued, and what you have spent since it. reconciliation: last statement as shown by the bank and reconciliation: spent since the last statement, as shown by the bank are damla's reserved words for that split, written when a card's figures are brought in from a screenshot of your bank app. when you set the amount still to pay on a card's details instead, the split is written under the same reserved opening. either way the total the card owes stays as it is. limit: damla counts these rows in an account's balance and in your forecast, but never as spending or income in your reports. related the activity list importing a statement the accounts page

title: Investments and holdings
summary: Shares, funds, gold: what you own, what it is worth, your gain.
text: the holdings screen lists what you own and have put a value on: shares, funds, gold and other metals, property, vehicles, and anything else you add. it answers two questions in one place: what your holdings are worth now, and what your gain has been. holdings: what you own and what it is worth. when to use it you own shares, funds, gold or another asset and want its value counted in your finances. you buy more of something, or sell some, and want the cost, the proceeds and the gain worked out. holdings live in insights, under holdings . the same items also appear under accounts, investments. step by step add a holding open insights , then holdings , then tap the add button (the plus sign). choose the type : stock or fund, property, vehicle, gold or other metal, or other. the type decides what the holding's page offers, such as a ticker field. enter the name, the currency, the units, and the value of one unit today. for a stock or fund, enter its ticker (for example wvra.l ) if you want its price looked up online. in what it cost (optional) , enter what you paid in total. leave it empty, or enter 0, for shares you received free, such as vested rsus. they cost nothing, so their whole value counts as gain. under paid from , choose an account if you are buying it now, or already owned if no account balance should change. keep the value current open the holding's page. under update the value , enter the quantity and the value of one unit, then tap save . to correct an old figure, go to values on file and tap the value. swipe one to delete a mistake. on the holding's page, tap what it cost to correct what you paid. this fixes the record; no account balance changes. tap more to rename it, change its type, or use buy more… and sell… . the newest value on file is the one in force, and a value you type beats a fetched one from the same day. until a holding has a value on file, its row reads at cost, no price yet and is valued at what you paid. buy more on the holding's page tap more , then buy more… . enter the units added, the price per unit today, and what you paid in total. the total fills in as units times price until you type your own; enter 0 for shares that vest or are granted free. under paid from , choose the account it was paid from, or no account (already paid, or free) . check the after this preview — units, total cost, average cost per unit — then tap save . sell on the holding's page tap more , then sell… . enter the units to sell (all of them is the default), the price per unit, any fees, and the date. choose money goes to : the account that receives the money. if it is in another currency, also enter the amount that actually arrived, so damla keeps both sides and the rate it implies. check the what this does preview — proceeds, fees, what you receive, the cost of these units and the gain or loss — then tap sell . the account receives the proceeds minus fees, and the fees are booked as a cost. the units sold take their share of the cost at the average cost per unit; the difference is booked as income in investment gains , or as a cost in investment losses . selling everything removes the holding from your investments and your net worth; its history stays. reading the report the hero card at the top of holdings shows what your holdings are worth ( worth now ) and your gain on investments , with a percentage when there is a cost to measure the gain against. below it: where it is : a donut chart of how the holdings are split, each slice labelled by name, share and value. each holding's row shows its value, and a small trend line once there are at least two values on file. gains and losses are shown with a sign and an arrow, and a percentage where one can be worked out — never by colour alone. limit: a vehicle is left out of the gain on investments: it loses value with age, so its page shows how its value changed since you last updated it, in grey, as a change rather than a loss. damla does not calculate tax, and it uses average cost rather than tracking purchases as separate lots. note: a holding in a currency damla has no exchange rate for is left out of the totals, and the screen says so. a pill at the top warns you when the oldest price on file is more than a week old. good to know price lookup is optional and off by default: with a ticker saved and the switch on, prices refresh about once a day, and only the ticker symbols are sent anywhere. see prices and exchange rates . a property with rent linked to it shows the rent received over the last 12 months and its gross yield. see property and cars . your holdings count towards your net worth at the value you gave them, not only at cost. see trends and net worth . related property and cars prices and exchange rates trends and net worth staged purchases

title: Property and cars
summary: Track things that lose or gain value with your own figures.
text: property, vehicles and other things you own — a gold ring, a plot of land — live in damla as holdings, with a value you keep up to date yourself. damla does not guess what they are worth: only shares and funds have a price it can look up. the figures shown are the ones you give, so your value is as current as your last update. damla gives you information and estimates about your own books, not valuations or advice. when to use it you own a home, an apartment, land or a car and want it counted in your net worth. you receive rent and want to see what it brought in and the yield against the property's value. you are buying something big with a loan and want the down payment, the loan and the instalments set up together. you want a record of how the value has changed since you last updated it. step by step add a property you own open insights , then holdings , then tap the add button (the plus sign). choose the type : property. name it, leave the quantity at 1, and enter the value of one unit today. in what it cost (optional) , enter what you paid if you want to see the gain against it. under paid from , choose already owned , so no account balance changes. holdings of other types, such as stocks or gold, are added the same way; see investments and holdings . link the rent you receive open plan , then income & bills , and tap the plus button. add the rent as income: the amount, the account it is paid into, and how often it repeats (every month, every 3 months, or custom… for a rhythm of your own). open the property's page and go to its rent section. choose what the rent is booked to. if nothing is linked yet, tap create “rent from …” and link it , and damla makes the income category and links it in one step. record rent as income in that category, or let a bank alert or a statement add it — damla adds up whatever is booked there. the property's page then shows rent, last 12 months and the gross yield on its value : that rent as a percentage of its value now. with less than a year of rent recorded, the page tells you the yield is understated. add a car financed by a loan open insights , then holdings , tap add and choose the type : vehicle. enter the name, the quantity 1 and the car's value. in what it cost (optional) , enter the full price. turn on financed by a loan . enter the amount financed . once both figures are typed, damla shows the down payment — the price minus the loan. choose the account the down payment comes from under paid from . enter the instalment, how often it repeats, the number of instalments, the date of the first one, and the account that pays them ( instalments paid from ). when you save, the down payment leaves your account, a loan is created for the rest, and its instalments go into your forecast and stop after the last one. the car and the loan count once each in your net worth: the car's value and the loan's debt. reading the value a holding with no value recorded yet is shown at cost until you enter one. every value is dated, and each holding keeps its history: the page has a value over time chart and a values on file list, where the newest value is the one in force. a vehicle loses value with age, so damla does not show a loss against what you paid. its page shows how its value changed since your last update, worded as a change and shown in grey, and a vehicle is left out of the gain-on-investments figure. gains and changes are always shown with a sign and an arrow, not by colour alone. tip: you set the rhythm for updating a value: type a new one whenever you have a figure you trust. the worth shown is always the newest value on file, and the change shown is measured against the value recorded just before it. good to know an off-plan property you are paying in stages is set up differently, as a staged purchase. when it is handed over, the purchase's page has handed over: move to investments : you enter the market value, it becomes a holding worth that value, and what you paid stays as its cost. see staged purchases . the instalments of a loan taken out on a financed holding are part of your forecast. to see how your balance moves over the weeks ahead, see forecast and safe to spend . property sits in the same list and the same totals as your other holdings. related investments and holdings staged purchases forecast and safe to spend trends and net worth

title: Staged purchases
summary: Off-plan property or anything paid in stages.
text: a staged purchase is damla's record of something you pay for in dated stages, such as an off-plan apartment. it shows what you have paid and what is still to come. payments still ahead go into your forecast, so the money is ready when each stage falls due. staged purchases. when to use it you are buying off-plan property and the developer asks for payments on known dates. you are paying for anything else in stages, such as a plot of land or a big order paid in parts. you have already paid something towards it, such as a down payment, and want it counted. you want the property to become a holding in your net worth when it is handed over. where to find it open plan , then staged purchases . you can also reach a staged purchase from accounts under assets . step by step create one on the staged purchases screen, tap add (the plus button). enter a name, the developer or seller (optional), the total price , and the account you usually paid from . under paid before damla , enter what you already paid under already paid and its paid on date. it counts as paid, and no account balance changes. under payments still to come , add each dated payment you know about: a due date and an amount . tap add another payment for each further one. tap save . the purchase's page shows a paid so far card with a progress bar, the price, what is paid, what is scheduled , and what is not yet scheduled . keep it up to date open the purchase. tap a payment to change its date or amount, or swipe it to delete it. to add one, tap add a payment . tap the price row to change the total price. if you forgot a payment you made before you started using damla, use the already paid before damla section: enter the amount and the date, then tap save . when you pay an instalment from an account, use record a payment : enter the amount, choose paid from , and tap save . recorded payments settle the oldest scheduled payments first. each payment in the list shows its date and amount and what is still outstanding: paid when nothing is left, or the outstanding amount in red with due now when it is overdue. hand over on the purchase's page, tap handed over: move to investments . enter today's market value in the value of the property field. damla tells you how much of the scheduled payments will be removed from your forecast, or says nothing is left to pay. tap move to investments to confirm. the purchase stops being a staged purchase and becomes a holding: what you paid stays as its cost, and the market value you entered becomes its worth. see property and cars . good to know note: payments still to come are counted in your forecast on their dates, along with your bills and income. after handover those scheduled payments leave the forecast, and the property is counted at its value instead. tip: enter only the payments you know about. you can add the later stages when the developer announces them. to change a date or an amount, tap the payment. limit: the figures on the page come from what you entered: the total price, the payments you scheduled and the payments you recorded. if a stage changes, tap the payment and correct it. note: damla gives information and estimates from your own books. it does not give financial or investment advice. related property and cars forecast and safe to spend instalment plans loans

title: Prices and exchange rates
summary: What Damla looks up online, when, and how to type your own.
text: market data is the only look-up damla does on its own: exchange rates for the currencies you use, and prices for the holdings you choose to track. both are optional, and damla works fully offline. when to use it you have an account or a card in another currency and want the rate it is converted at to stay current. you track a stock or fund and want its price fetched instead of typing it each time. a rate or price looks wrong, and you want to see what a refresh brought, or type your own for the day. what is sent, and nothing more for rates, damla sends only currency codes. for prices, damla sends only the ticker symbols you set for your holdings. no amounts, names or personal data are sent. a bank-name logo search elsewhere in the app runs only when you tap it. when it refreshes about once a day: when you open the app if the data is older than a day, and again when you come back to it after a day. in the background while the app is closed, when ios allows it. ios decides if and when this happens, so the refresh on open is the one to rely on. whenever you tap refresh now in settings, with a short minimum wait between taps and a longer one after failures. each source is fetched on its own: if one fails, the other keeps its data. step by step switch prices on open the holding's page and enter its ticker. you can also set tickers in settings, currencies and prices , under tickers . turn on look up prices for holdings (in the same settings page, under market data ). price lookup starts off. check a refresh, or type your own value open settings, then currencies and prices . tap refresh now . a report titled what changed lists each source — exchange rates and prices — each marked updated , skipped or failed : - updated , with a line per item: the new rate or price, and what it was before (or new , or unchanged ). - skipped , with the reason: price lookup is off, no tickers are set, daily rate updates are off, or you only use your main currency. - failed , with the error. if a service is busy, wait a moment and try again. the end of the report shows what the refresh did to your numbers: net worth and the lowest point in 90 days, before and after. under exchange rates , each foreign currency shows the rate in force and whether it was fetched or is your rate , with its date. to set your own rate, type it under set your own rate and tap save . under the toggles, damla shows when each source was last updated, or never updated ; the prices line also shows off while price lookup is switched off. which value wins the newest rate or price is the one in force. a rate or price you type wins on the day you enter it. the next refresh replaces it with a newer fetched one. the report says when your own value is still being used. prices quoted in pence are converted to pounds. good to know note: card purchases in another currency are estimated from the latest exchange rate plus your bank's markup, 2.5% when you have not set one, and marked with ≈ until the statement makes the amount exact. the markup is set in settings, currencies and prices , under card purchases in another currency . limit: an automatic refresh runs at most once a day. beyond that, refresh only when you tap refresh now . if the rate or price did not change after a refresh, read the report: it says what was updated, skipped or failed, and whether a value you typed today is still being used. note: rates come from exchangerate-api.com. prices come from a public quote service. note: damla gives information and estimates from your own books. it does not give investment or financial advice. related investments and holdings credit cards privacy and your data troubleshooting

title: Forecast and safe to spend
summary: How Damla works out the amount that is safe to spend, and how to read the chart.
text: the forecast shows your balance for the days ahead, day by day, from what is already in your books. safe to spend is the most you can spend today without your balance falling below your minimum at any point in the coming period. the forecast. when to use it to see how low your balance gets, and when, over the range you pick: 3m, 6m, 1y, 2y or 5y. when today says you may run short, to find the day it happens. after you change an income, a bill or a due date, to see what the weeks look like now. step by step open the forecast from the chart on the teal card at the top of today. pick a range with the picker at the top; the chart draws your balance for it, with your minimum as a dashed red line. touch and drag along the chart to move the dot. a small box shows the day's date, balance and movements, and the card below lists them as money in and money out with totals. read the banner at the top: if and when the balance would fall under your minimum, or that it stays above your minimum. tap what if at the top right to try a change: spend, receive, skip a recurring payment or plan, or add an instalment plan. you see the effect on safe to spend and the lowest point. nothing is saved to your books. how the number is worked out income and bills from plan, income & bills are counted on their schedules; ones you recorded or skipped are not counted again. card bills: an issued statement uses its real amount on its due date. a statement not issued yet uses a typical month of the card's spending - an average of its recent months, the number set in settings under expected card spending, or the figure you give in the card's details. an issued statement's real amount takes over. each card's figure is listed in the cards group under what this forecast is made of. instalment plans, staged payments, bills announced by notices and repayments with people are counted on their dates. everyday spending from your bank accounts is not estimated; your buffer covers it. safe to spend looks at least as far ahead as the look ahead setting, counting your next income inside that period too, so a big payment just after payday lowers the number. it is the lowest balance in that period minus the minimum. a worked example an invented household, on 9 november. currency aed, minimum balance aed 1,000, look ahead at least 30 days. what counts value everyday account (bank) aed 29,600 today savings aed 40,000, marked not in forecast internet, monthly on the 12th aed 350 out rent, monthly on the 16th aed 8,000 out salary, monthly on the 27th aed 25,000 in today shows: balance today aed 29,600, lowest point aed 21,250 on mon 16 nov, safe to spend aed 20,250 - the lowest point minus the aed 1,000 minimum. the window runs from 9 nov to 9 dec, past the salary on fri 27 nov, so what lands after payday is counted too. the savings are not in these figures. balance day by day (expected line; cautious is the same here, as every item is fixed): date balance why 9 to 11 nov aed 29,600 12 nov aed 29,250 internet 350 16 nov aed 21,250 rent 8,000 (the lowest point) 27 nov aed 46,250 salary 25,000 one-off payment limits (one payment, keeping the minimum): payment date most you could pay comfortable amount 10 nov, 13 nov or 19 nov aed 20,000 aed 16,000 29 nov (after salary) aed 36,500 aed 29,500 before the salary, a payment up to the first row's amounts never takes the balance under the aed 1,000 minimum. after payday, the limit is larger. good to know note: the chart draws two lines, expected and cautious. cautious delays or discounts income that is not fixed; safe to spend uses that line. outflows are never delayed, and an estimated amount is counted at its less favourable end. when nothing in your plan is uncertain, the lines overlap. limit: if a card has no estimate at all, a warning appears above the chart and the forecast is too optimistic: it leaves out what the card will spend after its next statements. give the card a typical month in its details, or import statements. if expected card spending is off in settings, only what is already on your cards is counted. money left out because its account is not in the forecast is named at the top. note: information and estimates, not financial advice. related what if income and bills that repeat ask damla a day with damla

title: What if
summary: Try a purchase, a loan or a late payment before you do it.
text: what if is where you try a change before you make it: spend an amount on a date, receive one, leave a payment out, or take on an instalment plan. damla compares your forecast with and without the change, so you can see what it would do to your lowest point and your safe to spend before you commit. what if: try a change before you make it. when to use it you are thinking of a big one-off purchase and want to know what it does to the weeks around it. you are considering an instalment plan and want to see the monthly payment in your forecast before you agree to it. an income might arrive late, or you might skip a bill, and you want to see what that costs you. money is expected on a date that is not in your books yet, and you want it counted. step by step open the forecast from the your balance ahead chart on today, and tap what if at the top right. tap add a change . choose the kind at the top: spend , receive , skip or instalments . for spend or receive : name it under what , enter the amount , pick the date , and choose the account it is paid from or goes into . for skip : choose under leave out which recurring payment or plan to leave out — an income or bill, an instalment plan, or a staged purchase. for instalments : enter the monthly instalment , choose the number of months (from 2 to 60), pick the first instalment date, and choose the account it is paid from . tap add . the change joins the list under changes to try . read the result above it: lowest point and safe to spend , each shown as it was, with an arrow to what it becomes with your changes. check the warning line: if the changes would take your balance under your minimum, a red warning says by how much and on which date. if not, a green line says the balance stays above your minimum for the next year. to try another combination, swipe a change to remove it. tap done when you are finished. a worked example an invented household, on 9 november. currency aed, minimum balance aed 1,000, looking ahead at least 30 days. one bank account and one salary: what counts value everyday account (bank) aed 29,600 today internet, monthly on the 12th aed 350 out rent, monthly on the 16th aed
