8,000 out salary, monthly on the 27th aed 25,000 in with no changes, damla shows a lowest point of aed 21,250 on mon 16 nov and a safe to spend of aed 20,250. the question what if answers: what is the most you could pay as one payment on a given date, and still keep the aed 1,000 minimum? payment date most you could pay comfortable amount 10 nov, 13 nov or 19 nov aed 20,000 aed 16,000 29 nov (after salary) aed 36,500 aed 29,500 how to read it: the same payment has a lower limit before payday and a higher one once the salary on 27 november has landed. what matters is the lowest point the weeks after the payment reach, not the balance today. the savings in this household, aed 40,000, are in none of these figures, because that account is marked not in forecast. good to know note: what if is only a preview. nothing on the screen is recorded, and the changes exist only while it is open. closing it leaves your books exactly as they were. limit: the comparison looks a year ahead. if you remove a change and the result does not move, check that the change was added: it is listed under changes to try. tip: the starting numbers come from your forecast, so they are only as good as what is in it: your income and bills, your cards' due dates and your instalment plans. see forecast and safe to spend . note: the numbers are information and estimates from your own books, not financial advice. related forecast and safe to spend ask damla instalment plans income and bills that repeat

title: Ask Damla
summary: Ask in your own words whether you can afford a holiday, a car or classes.
text: ask damla is a question box in the plan tab that answers "can i afford this?" from your own forecast. you write the question the way you would say it. damla tells you the amount your money can carry, and what that answer rests on. ask damla. when to use it before you commit to a holiday, a wedding, a course or a home move, and you want to know what your forecast allows. when you are considering buying something with a loan and want the budget, the loan it can carry and the monthly payment. when something is paid over time (classes, a course) and you want to compare paying at once against spreading it. any time you would otherwise wonder "what happens if i spend that?" step by step open the plan tab and tap ask damla . tap the box marked "ask damla, in your own words" and write your question. you can also tap one of the ready questions under for example to fill the box. tap ask . read the answer. a card shows the headline amount; below it are the details and a section called what this rests on . if damla did not understand it, it says so. try naming the thing (a holiday, a car with a loan, classes), and add the date or the price if you know it. for spending or a payment plan, tap set aside for it if you want the answer turned into a goal: damla adds it with this amount and date, so it can work out what to put aside each month. how the answer is made damla reads your question on this phone to find what it is about, when you need the money and any price, term or interest rate you wrote. the model only reads the words; it never calculates. the answer is then worked out by ordinary code from your forecast: for a holiday or other spending: a comfortable amount and the most your forecast allows . comfortable means 80% of the most, so there is room for surprises. if you named a price, a pill says whether it fits comfortably, fits but tightly, or is more than your forecast allows. for a car or other loan: a comfortable monthly payment, the most a month allows, and the loan that payment carries over the term you choose. it also shows the down payment still possible and your budget in total. change the loan term in months with a stepper, or the yearly interest rate in its field. the answer updates as you change them. if you wrote a price, damla shows what that price looks like as a down payment plus monthly payments. for classes or anything paid over time: if you said the price, damla compares paying at once with spreading it into equal monthly payments. it shows each way with the lowest balance it causes, and recommends the fewest payments that keep your balance comfortable. if you did not say the price, it shows what you could pay a month over different numbers of months. what this rests on the answer uses your forecast: your income, bills, cards and typical spending, and the money already in your accounts. everyday spending from your bank accounts that is not already a bill is counted too, and the section says how much a month it assumed. below you also see the forecast's start date, your minimum balance and, when it matters, the balance on that date. limit: if there is not enough history to know your everyday spending yet, none is counted and the answer is optimistic. the screen says so when that is the case. note: if you did not say when you need the money, a month from now is assumed. questions about dates further than five years ahead cannot be answered; the screen tells you so. careful: even without the new spending, your forecast may run below your minimum balance on or after the date the money is needed. the answer then appears with an orange warning saying so, and by how much. good to know your question and your data stay on the phone. nothing leaves it. the answer is an estimate from your own numbers, not financial advice. the two numbers to compare are comfortable and the most. spend more than comfortable only if you accept a thinner margin for surprises. the answer changes as your books change, so you can ask again after adding income or bills. related forecast and safe to spend what if set aside income and bills that repeat

title: Income and bills that repeat
summary: Salary, rent and subscriptions: set them up once.
text: income and recurring bills is the list in plan of everything that repeats: your salary, your rent, your subscriptions. set each one up once, and the forecast counts it on its schedule. income and bills that repeat. when to use it you get paid on a regular rhythm and want it counted in the forecast. you have bills that repeat: rent, school, subscriptions. damla has noticed payments that repeat in your history and is offering them to you. a repeating payment has been recorded or skipped by mistake and you need to undo it. step by step open the plan tab and tap income & bills . tap add (and if nothing is set up yet, the screen offers add one ). choose the kind: bill or income . the kind control at the top of the form does this. enter a name, the amount, and the account it moves through ( paid from for a bill, paid into for income). if the amount changes, turn on amount varies and enter a lowest and highest amount instead of one figure. choose repeats : every month, every week, every 2 weeks, every 3 months, every 6 months, every year, custom… for any rhythm (every n days, weeks, months or years), or once . if it ends, turn on stops after a number of payments and set how many. the date field then reads first payment . for income, choose how sure : fixed: arrives on time , varies: use the lowest recent , or irregular: count only when received . tap save . keeping the list right the list is sorted with what is due soonest first, under income and bills sections. each row shows its name, its rhythm, and how it stands: due today or due tomorrow in orange when a bill is here, overdue in red when it has passed, or the next date. for income the same lines read expected today or expected tomorrow . found in your history at the top of the list, damla shows payments it has noticed recurring in your history with a steady amount and rhythm. each has an add button that puts it in your forecast; swipe one away and tap not a bill if it is not one. nothing is added from history without your tap. when a bill is due a bill or income due tomorrow, today or late, and not recorded yet, shows on today under due . a line under coming up opens the item behind it when there is one: a bill or income opens its page, a card bill opens its payment sheet, a staged purchase opens its plan. open the item to see when it is next due, then adjust the amount, date, account or category if this time is different. tap mark paid (or mark received for income). damla adds the transaction, marks that one done and moves the next due date on. it says what it recorded and closes the screen. turn on use these details from now on to keep a new amount or account for the next times too. tap skip this one if it did not come this time: it is marked done without recording anything. you can record early. if the next one is not due for more than a week, damla asks before recording ("yes, i paid it early" / "yes, i received it"), so a second tap does not record next month's by accident. if a payment for that amount is already in your books (from a bank text, say), the bill is treated as paid and no reminder shows. good to know note: recorded or skipped one by mistake? open the item and tap undo the last one… . it becomes due again, and you can remove the payment that was recorded for it or keep it. how sure matters for the cautious forecast line: fixed income is counted as you said it, varies uses the lowest recent amount, and irregular is only counted once it is actually received. the cautious line delays or discounts income that is not fixed. swipe a row and tap delete to remove it; use edit on its page to change anything about it. the item's page keeps a short recorded here section: the last payments recorded against it. a loan instalment you mark paid here pays the loan down; it is not counted as spending. related forecast and safe to spend bills coming set aside credit cards

title: Bills coming
summary: How a bill announced by a message is remembered and then settled by the card charge.
text: bills coming is where damla keeps a bill from the moment a message announces it ("your bill is ready") until the charge that pays it arrives. the announcement itself is not spending: no money has moved. the card or bank charge that pays the bill is the one real transaction, and it settles the bill here, so nothing is counted twice. bills coming. when to use it a utility or other provider sends a "your bill is ready" message and you want it remembered without recording it as spending. you want to see everything announced but not yet charged, with amounts and due dates. a bill was noted by mistake and you want to take it away. step by step let the bill notice reach damla through your shortcut automation (or paste the message into add by sentence ). open the plan tab and tap bills coming . the page's title reads bills ; today shows a notice with the words bills coming that opens this same list. tap a bill to see its details: the amount, the due date, the customer account it is for, the breakdown, and, once known, which card or account usually pays that provider. when the charge arrives (a card alert or a statement row), damla matches it to the bill and the bill moves down to paid . you do not have to do anything. check the settled transaction in activity: when the bill had a breakdown, the provider's charge now carries the bill's categories. how the bill settles the matched charge is the one transaction for the bill. if the bill's breakdown adds up exactly to its total, that one charge is split across categories by the breakdown lines. electricity, water, cooling, gas, internet, phone and sewerage go to bills & utilities (or utilities if you have no such category). housing goes to housing (or rent , or bills & utilities ). a line none of these fits keeps the category the charge was filed under. the bill is then marked paid, and damla remembers which card paid that provider. reminders of the same bill ("is due", "overdue") only refresh the bill's due date; they never add a second one. once damla knows which card pays a provider, an open bill from that provider is already in your forecast: for a card, the cash leaves the account that pays that card on the card's due date, not when the notice arrived. where to see it today : the notice with the words bills coming opens this page. plan, bills coming : the same bills, each with its breakdown and what has been paid. when the open bills are all in one currency, a card at the top totals them. settings, recent alerts : each notice and reminder, with the reason it was noted. the forecast (from today, your balance ahead ) shows the bill as a payment when the paying account is known. the shape of a bill the bills and amounts you see are your own, so no worked figures are given here. the shape is this: a notice arrives with a total and an optional breakdown; the bill waits under coming ; one charge pays it; the charge is split across the breakdown's categories; the bill moves to paid . good to know careful: the first charge from a provider may not match its bill if the card statement gives the company a very different name than the bill message does. the charge is then added as an ordinary transaction. you can correct its category in activity. note: a wrongly noted bill can be undone in settings, recent alerts : the bill is forgotten and no transaction was involved. a mistake caught before any charge arrives can also be swiped away in plan, bills coming . limit: a charge is matched only while the window runs: from just before the notice arrived until up to 45 days after the due date, for the same amount and the same business. a different bill, or a charge months later, is not matched. until it is charged, a bill is not a transaction: the spending reports do not count it. if you undo the alert that added a settled charge (in settings, recent alerts), the transaction is deleted and the bill is owed again. if the bill repeats, set it up in income & bills instead: anything there that repeats every 3 months or less often is counted in set aside, which works out what to put aside each month. related income and bills that repeat how automatic capture works what damla ignores, and undoing an alert credit cards

title: Payees and categories
summary: How Damla learns where money goes and how to change it.
text: a payee is the shop, company or person money went to. a category is the bucket its spending or income goes into, such as groceries or salary. this page explains how damla files each payee the first time, what it remembers afterwards, and how you change any of it. when to use it a bank alert or pasted message was filed in the wrong category, and you want the next ones right. you want a category of your own, or a better name or icon for one. you imported a statement and damla is asking "who are these?" about some rows. you want to check how entries are being sorted before you trust the insights tabs. step by step tap the gear icon on the today screen to open settings, then tap categories . at the top, pick which list you want with the switch: spending or income . tap add to make a new category. type the name . the icon follows the name as you type: many kinds of spending (gym, pets, kids, insurance, repairs and more) get a matching picture on their own. to choose your own picture, tap one in the grid headed icon . the text under the name field then reads "your own icon. pick another, or tap the same one to go back to the suggestion." tap save . tap cancel to leave without saving. on this same screen: tap any category to rename it or change its icon on the same sheet. it is the same sheet in both places, titled new category or category . swipe a category and tap remove to retire it. you can also make a category on the spot: under the category picker in any entry form, tap new category… . it is selected right away. how damla learns a payee when you save a transaction that has a payee in a category, damla records the pair. the next alert or message from the same shop or person is filed in that category by itself, with no question. two habits make this work: fill in the payee field. the entry form labels it paid to (optional) for spending and from whom (optional) for income. if the kind of payment changes, save it in the new category. if earlier transactions from the same payee sit in a different one, damla asks before touching them: "change the other n payee ?" with change them to \<category\> or only this one . it explains that from now on new ones go to the new category by themselves. damla makes an exception for the catch-all: when you save in the form and the category is other (or other income for income), the pair is not remembered. an entry left there teaches it nothing. during an import: one question per payee when you import a statement (a csv file, a pdf or a screenshot), damla groups the rows into unknown payees, so you answer once per payee, not once per row. the section is headed who are these? (n left) , and it is answered before anything is imported. each question shows the payee's name, how many rows it covers, one example line, and a total of the money in or out. tap choose… on it and pick from: one of your existing categories (the list matches the direction of the money), use suggestion: … , the pick damla proposes, a credit card of mine , when the rows are payments to a card, another account of mine , when it is money moving between your own accounts, a property or asset i am paying for , a person (lend/borrow) , do not import these , to leave the rows out. suggestions come from plain wording rules for common lines: salary, cash withdrawal, bank charges, commission, emi, direct debit, interest and so on. where the iphone supports apple intelligence, the on-device model may also propose a category. it reads the payee's wording, a few example lines, how many rows the payee covers, and whether the money mostly came in or went out — never balances or amounts. the code checks what the model says before using it. a card number in the payee text, or your own name from the statement header, is matched by code, not by the model. your answer counts as the truth for those rows, and damla keeps the learned pairs for next time. good to know where two learned patterns both fit, the longest match wins, so "xyz grocery" beats a plain "grocery" rule. categories are yours to shape: nothing in the app depends on a particular name. removing a category takes it out of your pickers. old entries keep their category. the one category the app needs by name for instalment plan fees is recreated on its own if it is missing. the model step is optional and runs on your device. if the device cannot run it, the wording rules still do the job, and everything waits for your tap. damla gives information and estimates. which category money belongs in is your own bookkeeping. related fill a form type a sentence importing a statement where the money went

title: Set aside
summary: Yearly bills and goals: how much to put away each month.
text: set aside is one screen in the plan tab. it totals up the money a steady month should hold back for costs that do not come every month: bills that arrive now and then, and goals you are saving towards by a date. when to use it a bill comes every 3 months, 6 months or once a year, and you want to spread it over the months. you are saving towards something with a date: a holiday, a deposit, a new car. you want the safe-to-spend line on today to show how much is already set aside for goals. you want one number to put aside a month. step by step make sure the bills themselves are known: open the plan tab, tap income & bills , and add each bill that repeats every 3 months or less often, with a fixed amount (every 3 months, every 6 months, every year, or custom… for any rhythm). open the plan tab and tap set aside . the card at the top, put aside each month , shows the total to hold back monthly, with the line "so the bills and goals below are covered when they arrive." under bills that come now and then , each bill from income & bills is listed with its amount and rhythm on the left and its "a month" figure on the right, plus the next date it is due. under goals , tap add (the plus button) to save towards something. in the new goal form, give the goal a name , a target amount, and the date it is by . below, under saved , put anything you have already saved in saved so far . tap save . the goal's row shows how much is in and the target, with a progress bar, and either "reached" or its "a month" figure until the date you chose. to add money later, tap the goal's row and use put in more . a goal you no longer want has delete this goal in its own sheet. how the monthly figure is worked out damla divides what is still to save by the calendar months left until the due date, and rounds up to the next whole unit. part of a month still counts as a month, and there is always at least one. for bills that come now and then, the whole amount is still to come and the date is the next due date. the figure is recalculated from today's date each time, so it changes as the next due date moves. the total at the top is every bill's figure plus every goal's figure. limit: these are your own figures, not advice. damla shows what a steady month should put aside; whether a target or a date is right is your decision. good to know damla does not move money. the goal form says: "damla does not move money: this is what you have set aside for it, wherever you keep it." record real transfers as ordinary moves between accounts, and tap put in more to keep the goal's progress up to date. on today, money you have marked as saved towards a goal is shown as spoken for on the safe-to-spend line: "x of it is set aside for goals: y free to spend". safe to spend itself does not change: the money is inside your accounts, and the line only separates it out. only goals and bills in your main currency are listed on this screen. a bill appears here only if it is an outflow with a fixed amount and a rhythm of 3 months or longer. a bill marked amount varies, or a monthly one, stays in income & bills and the forecast instead of being set aside. change a bill in income & bills and this screen follows it. set aside stores no bills of its own, so there is nothing to edit twice. related income and bills that repeat forecast and safe to spend a day with damla title: Instalment plans
summary: Spread a card purchase over months and see the effect.
text: an instalment plan is a card purchase your bank lets you pay off month by month, kept in damla as dated payments rather than one large bill. you find the plans in the plan tab under instalment plans , and the forecast charges each payment on its due date until the plan is done. instalment plans. when to use it your bank has approved turning a card purchase into instalments and gave you the numbers. a statement already shows instalment rows (an "emi 2 of 6" line and the like), and you want the rest counted. you want to see the instalments end on their own and the card return to normal. a purchase was fully refunded or the bank recall ended the plan. step by step make sure the purchase is recorded as a card purchase, either by hand or from a bank alert. open the activity tab, find the purchase, swipe it right and tap turn into instalments . the screen is titled turn into instalments , with the purchase and its amount at the top under purchase . fill in the numbers as your bank states it : the monthly instalment , the number of months (2 to 60, with a stepper), a plan fee in total (optional) , and the date of the first instalment . tap convert . damla shows the plan in the plan tab under instalment plans : what is still to pay, a line like " monthly instalment × months months · n left · card name ", and "costs x extra in total" if there is a fee. to try a plan without committing it: in the plan tab, open what if , tap add a change , pick the instalments kind, and fill in a name, the monthly instalment , the months, the first date, and the account it would be paid from. the plan becomes real only when you convert it. telling damla in a sentence you can also type it. a sentence that mentions instalments, emi or taksit can bring up the same questions ("what is the monthly instalment?", "how many months?"). because a plan is a commitment, damla shows the result under check and save first: the plan's name, the instalment and months, the first date, and the fee if any. nothing is written until you tap create plan , which sits under the note "this creates a commitment, so please check it." if a purchase is already on a plan, damla says "that purchase is already on instalments." from a card statement when an imported card statement has rows that show which payment they are (emi 2/6, instalment 3 of 12, taksit 02/06 and the like), the import lists them under instalments found . nothing is added until you confirm. the rows are filed under the category instalments , not as everyday spending, and stay a charge in that statement's bill. the payments still to come join your plan on the card's later due dates. on each later statement, the next number appears, the plan moves forward, and no payment is counted twice. the plan leaves the forecast by itself after the last payment. how the money is worked out use the numbers from the bank's offer. the footer on the form says: "damla does not guess interest rates." the plan's figures follow from what you state: each payment in between is the instalment you stated. the last payment is whatever makes all the payments add up exactly to the total. the total is the first of these that applies: a total your bank stated, otherwise the purchase plus the stated fee, otherwise the instalment times the months. the extra cost of the plan is the difference between that total and the purchase. damla checks the stated numbers: the term must be at least 1 month, the instalment and the purchase above zero, and all amounts in one currency. if the numbers leave nothing for the last payment, damla refuses and says why. a stated total that differs a lot from the instalment times the months is kept as a warning on the plan. a plan always needs your ok before it is written, so you can check the numbers there. good to know the original purchase stays in your books as the spending it was, on the day it happened. the plan adds each payment on its due date until it ends. instalment payments are left out of the estimate of a card's typical month, so they are never counted twice. each payment reaches the forecast as its own dated payment and stops by itself after the last one. a plan taken from a statement runs on the card's own later statement due dates; a plan you set up yourself runs monthly from the first instalment date you gave. swipe the plan's row and tap cancel plan when the bank ends or recalls it, for example when the purchase was fully refunded. payments after that day are no longer counted, and the row shows cancelled instead of what was left. a plan made from a statement follows the bank's own numbering, so it stays in step even if you never entered it by hand. these figures describe a payment schedule the bank has offered. whether to take the plan, and what it costs you, is your decision, not advice. related the activity list credit cards forecast and safe to spend what if

title: Where the money went
summary: Spending by category, this month and last.
text: where the money went is damla's spending report. it shows what you spent, what you earned and what was left over, over the range you pick, by month and by category. where the money went. when to use it you want to see this month's biggest costs, and how they compare with last month. you want to see a year of spending by month, to spot the heavy seasons. you corrected a transaction and want to check how your reports changed. you want to see what came in as well as what went out, in one screen. step by step open the insights tab (the fourth of the five tabs). tap where the money went at the top of insights. the row already shows this month's spending, and last month's. pick a range at the top: this month , last month , 3 months or 12 months . under range , use count spending to choose which day a cost belongs to. read the big card: spent for the range, with earned and left over beside it. scroll for the charts and the lists, described below. how spending is counted two pickers sit at the top of the report: range, and count spending. when paid counts each cost on the day the money left. a card purchase counts on the day you used the card, not on the day you paid the card bill. this is the usual view of what happened. when it applies spreads yearly or prepaid costs over the months they cover — the months you gave the entry as the period it pays for. a period that starts on the first day of a month and ends on the last day of a month counts in equal parts. any other period counts in proportion to the days in each month. this is the usual view for comparing months, so one unusual payment does not dominate a month. note: the picker changes the spent figures only. income always counts on the day it came in. what is on the screen spent card: the total spent in the range, with earned and left over (earned minus spent) beside it. by month : a bar chart of spending, one bar per month. it appears when the range holds spending or income in more than one month. a donut chart: how the spending splits across categories, biggest portions first. it appears when there is more than one spending category. spending by category : a list with each category's total and its share of spending as a percentage, biggest first. categories with subcategories show their parts underneath. income : what came in, by income category. this section appears only when the range holds income. spent for : money you recorded as spending for another person, listed by that person. this section appears only when you have recorded spending for someone. limit: if some amounts are in a currency damla has no exchange rate for, a warning on the card says "some amounts need an exchange rate and are left out". those amounts are missing from the totals until you add a rate. if nothing was spent in the period, the list says nothing spent in this period. one account at a time the same report also opens for a single account. on the accounts tab, open an account that shows a card — a bank, savings, wallet, credit card or loan. tap the card to flip it over, then tap spending on the back. the report then covers only the entries that touch that account, and the account's name is the page title. investments, staged purchases and people open their own screens instead. good to know you can add, rename and remove categories in settings under categories . tap add , tap a category and edit name , or swipe it and tap remove . the report follows your changes. card purchases count on the day you used the card, not when the statement was paid. moving money between your own accounts is never spending and never income. the donut draws at most the eight biggest categories. any others still appear in the totals and in the list below. this report is a record of what happened. it gives information, not advice about what to spend. related budget trends and net worth payees and categories the activity list

title: Budget
summary: Monthly limits, or let Damla suggest them from your history.
text: the budget sets a monthly limit for each spending category and shows how the current month is going against those limits. damla suggests the limits from your past spending and cash flow, and you can change any figure before you accept it. budget. when to use it you want a monthly figure per category, worked out from what you actually spent, not a number from a template. you keep overspending in one or two categories and want a clear signal during the month, not at the end. you want to know how much room your income leaves after your usual spending and the commitments damla already knows about. you want a savings target as a share of your income. step by step open the insights tab and tap budget . if you have no budget yet, the screen says no budget yet and offers suggest a budget . if you already have one, tap ask for a fresh suggestion . on the suggested budget screen, set keep about … % of income with the slider. it starts at 10 percent, moves in steps of 5 and goes up to 40. check the summary: typical monthly income , already promised monthly (instalments and staged purchase payments, as a monthly average; the line is hidden when nothing is promised) and left after this budget . read the notes under worth knowing , if any. change any limit by typing in the field beside its row. tap use this budget to accept, or cancel to leave with nothing set. nothing is set until you accept a suggestion. note: moving the slider clears any figures you have typed in, so set it first and then adjust the rows. how the suggestion is made damla looks back at your complete months of recorded spending — up to six of them — and takes the middle of each category's monthly amounts as its usual figure. the suggestion starts there. a category is a steady cost when it has been present in at least three months since it first appeared and its amounts vary by no more than a fifth of their average. steady costs are not trimmed. any other category is flexible . flexible categories are trimmed only as far as needed to reach the savings goal, and never by more than 35 percent each. the savings goal is the share of income you set with the slider. the footer says how many full months of your history the suggestion is based on. if there is no history to work from, the screen says not enough history yet and asks you to import a statement or record some spending first. note: with fewer than three full months of history, one of the notes says the suggestion is a rough guide. adding earlier statements sharpens it. when a budget is in place once you have accepted a budget, the budget screen shows: left to spend this month : the total of all limits minus what you have spent so far this month, with a progress bar and the line "x of y · day n of m". by category : each limit with what you have spent so far. a red bar and "over by …" mean you have passed the limit. an orange bar and "spending faster than the month is passing" mean you are more than 15 percent ahead of the month's pace. under the progress are two buttons: ask for a fresh suggestion and remove this budget . good to know the budget sets limits for spending categories in your main currency. it does not move money, create accounts or block anything. income for the suggestion is what actually came in over your history. if nothing was recorded, it falls back to the income you set up in the plan tab, and a note says so. typing 0 in a limit field drops that category from the budget you accept. emptying the field does not: it falls back to the suggested figure. notes under worth knowing point out a forecast dip below your minimum balance, a category that was unusually expensive last month, or a shortfall no amount of trimming can close. if your history shows you spending more than you earn, a note names the monthly gap. the budget reports what you have spent against what you set. it is not financial advice. related where the money went income and bills that repeat instalment plans forecast and safe to spend

title: Trends and net worth
summary: Net worth today and over time, spending month against month, the monthly review.
text: insights has two screens for the long view. net worth shows everything you own minus everything you owe, today, in your main currency. trends draws net worth over time, month against month of spending, and a review of one month. net worth, with a link to its history. trends. when to use it you want one number for what you are worth, with the pieces that make it up. you want to see whether that number is moving up or down across the months. you want to compare this month's spending with last month, category by category. at the end of a month, you want to look back at what came in, what went out and what was saved. net worth open the insights tab and tap net worth . the row on the insights screen already shows the figure, with what you own and what you owe. the top card shows you are worth , with you own and you owe beside it. below it is the row see it over time , which opens trends on its net worth tab. if you still owe money on staged purchases, they are listed under promised, not yet paid , each with its due date. a line after these commitments follows them, showing what net worth would be once they are paid. they are not counted as debts in the top figure. the everything section lists your accounts, holdings, assets and debts, each with its amount in your main currency, or in its own currency when there is no rate for it yet. a holding shows its valuation as a number of units times a unit value, with the as-of date. it shows · out of date when the value is stale. net worth counts investments and other assets at the value you gave them, not only at what you paid. an item that needs a rate you have not set is flagged "needs an exchange rate for" with the currency named. something unlikely to be repaid is left out, with the line "left out: unlikely to be repaid". note: net worth lives in insights, not on accounts. the accounts screen shows only the cash you can spend; net worth counts everything, including things you could not pay a bill with. trends tap trends on the insights screen — it opens on the monthly review tab. pick one of three tabs at the top. net worth a chart of net worth at the end of each month, ending with a point for today. it is drawn from your recorded transactions and the values you gave holdings, so it moves when you record something or update a value, and not by itself. a card on top gives the latest figure and how much it has changed since the earliest point, with a date. with fewer than two month ends to show, the screen says not enough history yet . spending a bar chart of spending by month, with the five biggest categories over those months coloured in and the rest gathered as other . up to six months are shown side by side. the last month is the month so far, so its figures cover only the days that have passed. underneath, this month against last lists up to eight of the biggest categories with what changed: an arrow and an amount, and a percentage where it can be worked out. a category with nothing last month says new this month . changes carry both a sign arrow and a colour, so you can read the direction either way. monthly review the review of one month — the last complete one first, or any of the months in the menu at the top. each part appears only when there is something to show: a saved card, or saved so far for the current month: what came in minus what was spent, and as a share of what came in when anything came in. came in , spent and, when there is an earlier month, last month spent beside it. where it went : the biggest categories of the month with their change against the month before. biggest expenses : the three largest single payments of the month, with dates. net worth over the month : how your net worth moved while it lasted. good to know all the figures are in your main currency, converted with the rates on file. an amount with no rate is left out of the totals until you set one. trends shows at most six months of month-by-month spending; the net worth chart reaches further back, one point per month end. the biggest-expenses list counts confirmed entries only, and leaves out reconciliation adjustments, so a correction made only to match a statement does not crowd out real spending. these screens give information about your own history. they are estimates and records, not financial advice. related where the money went budget investments and holdings the accounts page

title: What I noticed
summary: Patterns Damla finds in your history.
text: what i noticed is the page in insights where damla reports the patterns it has found in your own history: payments and income that repeat, and how the last three months went. in one tap you can turn what you already do into recurring entries, instead of typing each one by hand. what i noticed. when to use it you have been recording for a while and want damla to find the regular payments you have not entered yet. something keeps appearing in your history — a subscription, a fee, a salary — and you want the forecast to count it before it happens. you want a short summary of the last three months: your biggest cost, and whether you spent more than you earned. step by step open the insights tab and tap what i noticed . read the section regular payments i found . each row names the payee, and under it a line that says whether damla read it as income or as a bill , how often it repeats, and how many times it has been seen. look at the amount on the right of each row. it is a single figure, or a range when the amount varies from one time to the next. tap add on the row you recognise. the entry is added to your recurring items, and from then on the forecast counts it before it happens. the section ends with the line "adding them to plan lets the forecast count them before they happen." when there is nothing to report, the page says so: "nothing new. import more history and i will look for regular payments and income." regular rows appear as you record and import more. the last three months below the list, a section headed last 3 months sums up that stretch of your books. it names your biggest cost, with its total and its share of all spending as a percentage. it then adds one of two lines: either that you spent more than you earned, with the difference, or — when you earned something in that period — what you kept, and what share of what you earned that was. this section appears once your spending has at least one category. it reads the whole three months, from the start of the month before last to today, not this month alone, so one unusual week does not distort the picture. good to know nothing is added on its own. a pattern becomes a recurring entry only when you tap add . you choose each one. a row you leave alone shows again. there is no button that hides a pattern, so it comes back the next time you open the page. a pattern has to repeat. damla suggests something only when it has seen it three times or more, at even gaps — monthly, weekly, or every 2 weeks — with the last one recent enough that it still looks like it is going on. anything you already have under income & bills is not offered again. a range means an estimate. when the amount of a repeating payment varies, damla shows the spread it saw. check it against your own records before you add it. added entries live in plan. you can change or remove them later under plan , income & bills , like any other recurring entry. the summary follows your books. both parts are worked out from what you have recorded. correcting a transaction in activity changes what this page reports. this page reports what your history shows, in figures and estimates. it gives information, not financial advice. related where the money went income and bills that repeat forecast and safe to spend trends and net worth

title: How automatic capture works
summary: Bank texts, emails, Wallet payments and statements, and what Damla does with each.
text: automatic capture is how a bank message becomes a transaction without you typing anything. damla reads the texts, emails, wallet payments and statement files that reach it, works out what each one is, and then either adds it, asks you about it, or leaves it alone. how messages reach damla ios gives apps no access to messages or mail, so damla never reads them on its own. something reaches damla only when you send it, in one of three ways: a shortcut you set up passes each new text, email or wallet payment to damla as it arrives. the share sheet : you select a message and share it to damla. the file picker : you choose statement files to import. everything is read on the phone. nothing is uploaded. what happens to a message damla checks each message against the same list of rules, in this order, and stops at the first one that fits. one-time and approval codes are dropped. the words of the message are never stored, so a code cannot be read back later. all that stays is one line in the log saying "one-time code: never kept". a bill notice is remembered as a bill. "your bill is ready" is not a payment: the money has not moved. damla keeps it as an expected bill, and the card charge that pays it later is the one real transaction. adverts, limit and rate notices, reminders and announced future charges are skipped. they name an amount, but no money moved. when such a message is about money, damla logs its first words, so you can see a wrong call. a clear bank alert is added at once. a purchase, refund or income whose card or account digits match one of your accounts becomes a transaction straight away. card payments, refunds and transfers are recognised. the category comes from how you filed that payee before, falling back to other for spending and other income for money in. anything unclear waits in the inbox for one tap. nothing that creates a commitment — a bill, a loan, an instalment plan — is added without your confirmation. a message that is not about money at all is dropped. it is not kept and not logged, so a private message never lands in the inbox or the log. where to check what happened recent alerts (settings > bank messages and statements) is a log of the last 50 alerts, newest first, each with a short reason: added, waiting in the inbox (and why), already recorded, ignored, or a bill noted as coming. if a bank message arrives and nothing shows up here, the shortcut did not run. the inbox shows on today as n waiting for your ok . tap an item to open it in add by sentence , where it is read again for you to check. it leaves the inbox when you save it, and discard takes it out without adding anything. an alert damla acted on can be taken back: in recent alerts, swipe right on the line and tap undo . the transaction it added is deleted, or the bill it noted is forgotten. good to know the same alert twice is added once. a purchase reported again by the bank's text, its email or wallet shows as already recorded. a second report of the same amount within a few minutes waits in the inbox for you to decide. the first alert from a new card waits in the inbox , because damla does not know that card's last digits yet. complete it once and damla learns them. a message that arrives while the phone is locked waits, and is added the next time you open the app after unlocking the phone. if your books are read-only, it stays in that queue until you can edit again. a statement pdf sent by a shortcut is queued. today shows n waiting to review with the note "statements or screenshots. nothing is added until you confirm", and you review it before anything is added. where the phone has apple intelligence , the model may only read fields from the text. every number and name it returns must appear in the text or it is ignored, and what it reads is never saved without you seeing it. reading is by wording and is not perfect. an offer worded like a payment can occasionally get through, and an unusual wording can wait in the inbox instead of being added. limit each shortcut to your bank's sender or subject, so unrelated messages are never sent to damla. limit: experimental. automation depends on ios and can miss a message. check recent alerts now and then. nothing unclear is saved without your ok. related the automation setup wizard the inbox what damla ignores, and undoing an alert importing a statement settings > bank messages and statements > automations.

title: The automation setup wizard
summary: Settings > Automations > Set up step by step.
text: the setup wizard walks you through making the shortcuts automations that feed damla, one kind of capture at a time, and then watches for your first real alert to confirm it works. ios does not let an app create automations, so you make each automation once, by hand, in the shortcuts app, and the wizard guides you through each step and checks the result. the setup wizard: choose what damla should catch. when to use it you are setting up damla and want its automatic capture working, with the exact steps laid out for you. you want to add one more kind of capture — say, bank emails — and need the exact steps for it. an automation you made by hand never worked, and you want to redo it with the steps in front of you. step by step open settings , then bank messages and statements , then automations (shortcuts) , and tap set up step by step . on the first page, what should damla catch for you? , turn on what you want. each choice has a one-line explanation under it: - bank text messages — each new text from your bank is sent to damla; clear ones are added as transactions, and anything unclear waits for your ok. - bank emails — each new email from your bank is sent to damla and read like a text message. - statement pdfs by email — the pdf attached to an email is queued in damla, and you review it before anything is added. - apple pay payments — each apple pay or tap payment is added at once; one automation per card, for cards you added to apple wallet. - screenshot of your bank app — one tap on the back of the phone screenshots your bank app's transaction list and sends it to damla; you review the transactions before anything is added. tap continue . each kind you chose gets its own page, in turn. on each page, type the sender at the top and tap save , when the kind needs one: a sender name or number for bank texts; a sender email address (or part of it) for bank emails and statement pdfs; the last 4 digits of the card for apple pay. the screenshot kind needs no sender. the field starts with the first sender already saved for that kind, if there is one. read the numbered steps for the shortcuts app on the same page. you can select and copy the text of each step. tap open the shortcuts app and follow the steps there. or tap copy the apple intelligence prompt and paste the prompt into the shortcuts app's apple intelligence, to have it build the automation for you. the button says copied once the prompt is on the clipboard. tap next to go on to the next kind, or back to correct the one before. the last page is test it . send yourself a test: have the automation fire once, with a real text, email or payment from that sender, or run the shortcut. the page shows waiting for the first alert… until something arrives while you are on it, then a green tick with what damla received and the words you're set . tap done . not near your bank? tap i'll test it later and test when it suits you. if nothing arrives the is it working? section on the automations screen says whether anything has reached damla yet, and when the last bank message arrived. after you set one up, send yourself a test message. if it does not show in recent alerts within a minute, the automation is not running: check that it is set to run immediately . a statement or a screenshot does not appear in recent alerts — it waits for review instead. the wizard watches that queue too, and tells you when a statement has arrived to review. good to know the wizard itself creates nothing in shortcuts. it saves the senders you type, shows the steps and checks for the first alert. you make the automation once, in the shortcuts app. the steps and the prompt are the same ones shown on the automations screen , where you can also copy the steps as text and copy a sender. cancel and done close the wizard. the senders you saved along the way stay saved, and you can reopen the wizard whenever you like. the wording on your iphone may differ slightly from the steps. if damla's actions are missing in shortcuts , the automations screen lists the actions to look for — add to damla , add statement to damla , add card payment to damla , how much can i spend — and what to do: open damla, force-quit shortcuts and open it again; if an action is still missing, restart the iphone. limit: experimental. automation depends on ios and can miss a message. check recent alerts now and then. nothing unclear is saved without your ok. related how automatic capture works bank texts and emails apple pay and wallet payments troubleshooting

title: Bank texts and emails
summary: Send each bank message to Damla with a Shortcut.
text: a shortcut automation passes each new text or email from your bank to damla as it arrives, so purchases, refunds and income are recorded for you. you connect one bank at a time. damla shows you the exact steps, and you make the automation once in the shortcuts app. automations: the senders you added. when to use it your bank sends a text every time you spend, get paid or top up on a card or account. your bank also sends transaction alerts by email, and you want those recorded too. you want fewer payments typed in by hand. you want a record of what was sent to damla and what it did with each message. the actions damla offers in shortcuts damla's four actions appear in the shortcuts app when you add a new action: add to damla — has a text field and a source field (text message, email or wallet payment). add statement to damla — takes a statement pdf or a screenshot and queues it for review. add card payment to damla — takes a merchant, an amount and a card (see apple pay and wallet payments). how much can i spend — answers with your safe-to-spend estimate, worked out by the forecast code. the automations screen in damla lists these same names. in the shortcuts app, tap add action, then apps, then damla to find them. if one is missing there, open damla, force-quit the shortcuts app and open it again. if it is still missing, restart the iphone. step by step first tell damla who your bank is, then make the automation. open damla, then settings, then bank messages and statements, then automations (shortcuts). in the section "bank text messages" (or "bank emails"), type your bank's sender name or number and tap add. for an email, part of the sender's email address is enough. tap your bank's entry in the list to see the exact steps. use the copy buttons if it helps: one copies the steps, one a prompt for the shortcuts app's apple intelligence, and one your bank's sender name, so nothing is mistyped. follow the steps in the shortcuts app: tap automation, then the plus button, then choose message (or email). under sender, choose your bank. leave message contains empty. choose run immediately, then next. choose new blank automation, tap add action, search for add to damla and pick it. set its text to shortcut input, so the message itself is passed on. set source to text message (or email, so damla knows where it came from). tap done. switch notify when run off if it appears. tip: ios does not let damla create the automation for you; you make each one once in the shortcuts app. the prompt that automations copies is written for the shortcuts app's apple intelligence: paste it there and it can build the automation for you. what happens to each message a clear purchase, refund or income whose card or account digits match one of your accounts is added as a transaction at once. an unclear message, an unknown card, an instalment conversion or a statement notice waits in the inbox for one tap. nothing that creates a commitment is added without your confirmation. a bill announcement becomes an expected bill, not a transaction. one-time codes are ignored and never stored, even if the phone is locked. the same alert delivered twice is added once. note: the first alert from a card or account whose digits damla does not know yet goes to the inbox. complete it once and damla learns them: the digits are remembered on the account you pick. good to know send yourself a test message after setting an automation up. on the automations screen, the is it working? section shows when the last bank message arrived, and recent alerts lists recent alerts, each with what was done and why. if nothing shows within a minute, check that the automation is set to run immediately. a locked phone cannot open the books. damla keeps the text and adds it the next time you unlock the app. the wording in the shortcuts app may differ slightly from these steps on your iphone's software version. the names add to damla, text and source are the ones to look for. adverts, limit or rate notices and reminders from your bank are skipped on their own; see what damla ignores, and undoing an alert . related how automatic capture works apple title: Apple Pay and Wallet payments
summary: Add card payments as they happen.
text: when you pay with apple pay or tap your card, wallet knows the payment at once. a wallet transaction automation sends each payment to damla as it happens, so it is recorded for you. when to use it your cards are added to apple wallet and damla should record every payment as you make it. your bank's message about the payment arrives late, or not at all, and you want it recorded anyway. you want the merchant recorded as wallet reports it. which actions to use both of these are damla actions in the shortcuts app, and both do the same job: add to damla , with its text set to a one-line sentence about the payment and its source set to wallet payment. add card payment to damla , which takes the merchant, the amount and the card direct from the wallet transaction. the amount arrives with its currency already in it, so there is no separate currency field and no conversion is guessed. step by step one automation per card, for cards you added to apple wallet. open damla, then settings, then bank messages and statements, then automations (shortcuts). under "apple pay payments", type the last 4 digits of your card and tap add. tap the card's entry in the list to see the exact steps for it. you can copy the steps, or copy a prompt to paste into the shortcuts app's apple intelligence. open shortcuts, tap automation, then the plus button, then choose wallet transaction and pick the card. choose run immediately, then next. choose new blank automation, tap add action, search for add to damla and pick it. set its text to the sentence the steps show you: purchase of [amount] with card ending (your digits) at [merchant]. damla has already written your card's digits into that sentence, so only amount and merchant are left in brackets. tap into the text field and insert the amount and the merchant from the wallet transaction where the brackets are. set source to wallet payment. tap done. tip: the sentence names the card by its digits, the same way a bank text does. if the digits match the last digits you saved for that card in its account details, damla files the payment under it straight away. if you prefer, use the add card payment to damla action instead of add to damla. its three fields — merchant, amount and card — take their values from the wallet transaction. what happens to each payment a payment on a card damla knows is added as a transaction at once. a payment on an unknown card, or anything damla cannot read, waits in the inbox for one tap. if the same payment also reaches damla from a bank text, it is recorded once. a second report with a matching shop name is answered already in damla . if the shop is named differently and it arrives within 15 minutes of the first, the second report waits in the inbox as a possible duplicate for you to discard. note: with the phone locked the books cannot be read, so damla keeps the payment and adds it the next time you unlock the app. good to know send a test payment through after setting up. the automations screen shows when the last message reached damla, and recent alerts lists each one with what was done. if it did not arrive, the automation is probably not set to run immediately. the digits matter. a card whose last digits you saved in its account details is matched automatically. a card damla does not know waits for you to tell it which one it was; you do this once per card. if damla is read-only because a trial or subscription has ended, the action says so and nothing is added until you subscribe again. related bank texts and emails how automatic capture
