title: Importing a statement
summary: PDF or CSV statements, checked against your balances.
text: importing a bank or card statement brings its transactions into your books in one go, checked against the balances the statement itself reports. use it to start damla with history, to catch up after a gap, or to make your books agree with the bank. when to use it you are setting up and want several months of history added at once. bank alerts missed some days, for example on a card or account you started using mid-month. you want to check your books against the bank: every transaction counted once, and the balances matching. step by step open accounts, tap the plus button, then import statements. choose the statement files (pdf or csv). you can import several accounts and months together. for each file, check what damla set up: the account name, whether it is a bank account or a credit card, and the currency. turn on "charges are printed as positive numbers" if the card prints its charges without a minus, and "dates are month/day (us style)" if your dates are written that way. review what damla found for each file: how many rows, whether it matches an account you already have, and the balance after the last row. if a statement does not state a balance, enter what that account holds (or owes, for a card) today, so the starting point can be worked out. answer each unknown payee once: choose a category, mark it as one of your own accounts, or skip it. every matching row follows your answer, and next time the payee is remembered. tap import. rows already recorded are skipped, so nothing is counted twice, and repeated rows from overlapping files are counted once. tip: open the rows skipped line on the review screen to see what each one was taken to be. a row that came in earlier as a bank alert counts as the same transaction when the amounts are the same, the shop names fit, and the dates are up to three days apart. banks post a few days later than they charge. good to know everything is read on the phone. the statement is never uploaded anywhere: there is no account and no server. locked pdfs ask for the password once. many banks lock their statements. damla asks for the password, and can keep it in this phone's keychain so the next statement from the same bank opens by itself. nothing is synced, and you can forget saved passwords in settings. debit and credit columns are read by position. when a statement prints a debit and a credit column, a refund and a purchase of the same amount look the same as plain text. damla therefore reads where each number sat on the page, under its column heading, before deciding the sign. where the iphone has apple intelligence, and a card statement's summary box is written in a way the rules cannot read , the on-device model reads only that summary box — not the transaction rows and not the whole file, and nothing leaves the phone. damla accepts nothing on the model's word: code checks that every figure it returned is printed in the statement, and that the summary's own arithmetic closes, before the figures are used. any figure that fails a check is dropped, not fixed. nothing is added until you confirm the import. on phones without apple intelligence, the transaction rows are still read; if the statement's balances are missing, damla asks you for today's figure instead. what happens at the end if every row is already in your books, the button reads reconcile to the statement and still makes the balances agree exactly. if you did not record some of the money one by one, it is filled in from the statement. earlier reconciliation adjustments inside that period are replaced. at most two clearly labelled adjustments are added: the balance brought forward and anything still missing at the end. both are reconciliation lines, not spending, and afterwards your books match the statement's opening and closing balances. if the statement does not state a closing balance, nothing is reconciled. rows that say which payment of how many they are (instalment markers on a card statement) are listed under instalments found, and nothing is added until you confirm. they go under the instalments category, not as spending. the payments still to come are added to your instalment plans on the card's later due dates. purchases in another currency are updated to the amount the bank really billed. limit: experimental. reading statements with apple intelligence is new and can get a row wrong. check the totals before you import. nothing is saved without your ok. related screenshots of your bank app starting balances and adjustments payees and categories bank texts and emails

title: Screenshots of your bank app
summary: Update from a screenshot of your bank app's transaction list.
text: damla can update an account from a screenshot of your bank app's account page or card page. your phone reads the text; the pictures are not kept. nothing is written until you check it and tap. when to use it you want to set or correct a balance quickly, without filling in forms. you are adding a card and want everything its bank page shows: what you owe, the last statement and its due date. you want to bring several accounts up to date in one go. you can pick up to ten screenshots at a time. step by step in your bank app, open the page that shows the amounts: the account page with the balance, or the card page with the amount owed, the last statement amount, its minimum and its due date. take a screenshot. in damla, tap the plus button, then update from screenshots . tap choose screenshots and pick one or several pictures. wait while damla reads each picture on the phone. you see reading… , then one section per account. check each section: which account the picture matches, or a new one with a suggested name and a bank damla recognised. you can edit a new account's name before saving. for a card, say the day the statement closes if damla asks, and say which account pays the card. tap add it for a new account, or update to match for one you already have. when the books already agree with the picture, the section says already matches your books . good to know tip: take screenshots of the page that shows the amounts. a page with only a list of transactions has no balance to read. what it reads. damla looks for labelled values, such as "available balance", "outstanding", "statement balance", "minimum due" and "due date", and takes the value next to the label. the longest matching label wins, so "minimum due" is never read as "due". the labels, and the on-screen text reading, work in english and turkish for now. the currency used is the currency code printed most often on the page. when no currency code is printed in capitals, damla uses your main currency. card pages. on a card page, a plain "balance" is what you owe. damla splits it into the last statement still to pay and what you spent since, and keeps the statement's due date if the page shows one. if the page shows only the limit and the available credit, damla works the owed amount out as the limit minus the available credit, and says so. naming a new account. a new account is named after the page heading (for example "neoplus"), with the bank name in front when the picture names one, and it gets that bank's logo. damla also keeps the last digits of an account or card number it can see on the page, so later bank alerts find the account on their own. when the books differ. each section shows the bank's figure beside damla's: bank shows and damla had for an account, owed now and damla had for a card. saving adds an adjustment that brings the account to what the bank shows: one for an account's balance, and for a card up to two, one for the last statement and one for what you spent since. an adjustment is not income and not spending. warnings. if something in the picture looks inconsistent — the total owed lower than the statement amount, or the minimum due higher than the statement amount — a warning line appears on the section, above the button. related importing a statement how automatic capture works the accounts page setting up your books

title: What Damla ignores, and undoing an alert
summary: Adverts, limits, reminders and codes are skipped; how to take back a wrong call.
text: damla records a bank message only when it says that money actually moved. adverts, limit notices, reminders and one-time codes are skipped. anything damla does act on can be undone from one screen. recent alerts: swipe right to undo. when to use it a message reached damla and nothing changed, and you want to know why. damla acted on a message it should not have, and you want to take it back. you have just set up a shortcut and want to see what damla does with each message. what damla skips messages like these are never recorded: one-time and approval codes ("otp", "verification code", "do not share"): dropped, and the message is not kept — not in your books, not in the log, and never written to disk. adverts and offers : wordings such as "cashback", "offer", "rewards", "congratulations", "apply now", "valid until". limit and rate notices : "limit has been", "limit is set", "limit increased", "interest rate". reminders : wordings such as "reminder", "don't forget", "kindly pay" and "pay by". amounts that have not moved : a number written right after "over", "above", "more than", "exceeding", "up to" or "minimum spend", or a sentence built on "if you" or "you can". that is an offer or a limit, not a charge. a transaction that did not happen : declined, unsuccessful, failed, rejected, insufficient. messages with nothing about money , such as a delivery notice: dropped, not kept, not logged. when a message about money is skipped, it is marked ignored . the log line carries its first words, never the whole message, so a wrong call can be seen later. not every skip leaves a line: a message that a shortcut handed over while your phone was unlocked, and that damla dropped, is not saved at all. one that arrives while the phone is locked is read when you next open damla, and that reading is kept. what is not skipped a message that says your bill is ready becomes an expected bill, not spending. the card or bank charge that later pays it is the transaction. a card statement notice (a total due together with a minimum due) is read as a statement and waits for you to review it. a reminder for a bill damla already noted does not add a second one: it refreshes that bill's due date, and the line says reminder of a bill already noted . anything unclear waits in the inbox for one tap. nothing that creates a commitment is added without you confirming it. checking what happened open settings, tap bank messages and statements , then recent alerts . read the list. each money message shows what was done and why: added , waiting in the inbox , already recorded , ignored or noted, nothing to record yet , plus how long ago. the list holds the 50 most recent lines. if a money message arrived and nothing is listed, the shortcut did not run. check the keyword, that it is set to run immediately, and that the text is the blue shortcut input pill. undoing an alert in recent alerts , swipe right on an alert damla acted on and tap undo . confirm. what is undone: - an alert that was added: the transaction it added is deleted. if that transaction had settled a bill, the bill is owed again. - an alert that was noted: the bill it noted is forgotten. the line stays in the list with "undone" in front, so you can see what happened. undo appears only on lines where damla acted on its own and the action is still in force: a transaction it added that is still in your books, or a bill it noted that is still open. lines marked already recorded , ignored or waiting in the inbox have nothing to take back. swiping the other way offers delete , which removes only the log line. clear all empties the list; transactions already added stay. good to know limit: reading is by wording and is not perfect. an offer worded like a payment can occasionally get through, and an unusual wording can wait in the inbox instead of being added. careful: a shortcut sends everything it is pointed at. limit it to your bank's sender or subject, so unrelated texts and mail are never sent to damla. related how automatic capture works bank texts and emails bills coming troubleshooting

title: Settings, page by page
summary: Where everything is in Settings.
text: settings holds the everyday controls: the lock, the minimum balance, reminders, market data, the automations and your backups. this page is a map, top to bottom. settings. when to use it you cannot remember which page a setting lives on. you want to know what a page does before opening it. step by step open today and tap the gear at the top right. that opens settings. tap a row to open that page; the back button returns. the pages, top to bottom from top to bottom, the list is the user guide , subscription , a basics section, then rows for the other pages. user guide step-by-step tutorials for everything in damla. the book icon on today opens the same guide. subscription the subscription lives on this page. see the free trial and the subscription . basics setting what it does ask for face id every time, or after 1, 5 or 15 minutes away. main currency the currency everything is added up in. it cannot be changed here. minimum balance the amount you want to keep untouched. enter it and tap save minimum . look ahead at least … days how far the forecast looks even when your next income comes sooner. anywhere from 0 to 90 days, in 5-day steps. expected card spending off, or the average of 3, 6 or 12 months; it fills in card bills for statements not issued yet. once a statement is issued, its real amount takes over. safe to spend is what remains above the minimum at your lowest point, so the minimum and the look-ahead both change it. reminders notify me before things are due : a notification the day before and on the day for bills, income and card bills that are due and not recorded yet. you choose the hour, from 06:00 to 22:00. warn me when my balance may dip below my minimum : one notification, worked out on this phone from your data. if you have switched notifications off for damla in the iphone's settings, a line here says so. currencies and prices market data : turn on update exchange rates daily and look up prices for holdings , or tap refresh now to fetch straight away. a manual refresh always tries the rates, and the prices only if that switch is on. after a refresh, a report shows what each source updated, skipped or failed. rows show when each source was last updated. card purchases in another currency : the bank's markup damla estimates with (2.5% when left empty), and how to read short currency words such as "dh" and "dhs" in your messages — as your main currency, or as aed or mad. exchange rates : one row per currency you use, with the rate in force, whether it was fetched or yours, and its date. you can type your own. tickers : one row per holding, to fetch its price. both look-ups are optional and the app works offline. details: prices and exchange rates . categories add categories, and rename or remove them. details: payees and categories . bank messages and statements automations (shortcuts) : how your bank's texts, emails and wallet payments reach damla, and the steps for each automation. recent alerts : what damla did with the messages that reached it, and where to undo one. see what damla ignores, and undoing an alert . statement passwords : passwords damla kept for locked statement pdfs, in this phone's keychain. forget … saved passwords removes them; with none saved, the section says no statement passwords saved. they never leave the phone and are not in backups. backup and your data automatic backup : once a day, when you leave damla, an encrypted copy goes to a folder you choose. the newest 7 are kept. export transactions : a csv of every transaction, for all years or one year you pick. tap make a csv file , then share to save or send it. export an encrypted backup : an encrypted file with a passphrase of at least 8 characters. keep the passphrase safe. restore from a backup : choose the file, enter the passphrase. it replaces all data on this phone. family : make a snapshot for family creates a read-only picture of today's numbers, encrypted with a passphrase you tell the other person. they open it in damla on their phone; it does not update. delete all data erases everything on this phone. it cannot be undone: export a backup first if you might need it. set-up guide restarts the set-up guide, so you can finish anything you skipped the first time. good to know note: everything on these pages happens on the phone, except the optional market data refresh, which sends only currency codes and ticker symbols. related backup and restore export and the family snapshot how automatic capture works the free trial and the subscription

title: Backup and restore
summary: Encrypted backups to a folder you choose, and how to restore.
text: a backup is a single encrypted file with everything damla holds: your accounts, transactions, plans and settings. you make one to keep your books safe, and to restore them if you delete the app. when to use it before you delete the app. deleting the app erases its data. before any big change to your records, or before installing a test or pre-release version of the app. when you want a copy damla makes every day, without being asked. when you want a complete copy of your books, held outside the app and in your hands. backups live in settings. open today, tap the gear at the top right, then backup and your data . everything under backup happens on the phone; you choose where each file is saved. step by step make a backup file open settings, then backup and your data . tap export an encrypted backup . type a passphrase of at least 8 characters and tap export . tap the share button that appears. save the file to files or icloud drive, or send it to your mac. careful: the passphrase is the only key to the file. nobody, including damla's developer, can open the backup without it, and damla cannot recover it. keep a copy of the phrase somewhere safe, separate from the file. note: restoring replaces everything on this phone with the backup. you cannot merge a backup with what is already there. restore a backup open settings, then backup and your data . tap restore from a backup and choose the damlabackup file. type that backup's passphrase. damla warns you that this replaces all data on this phone. tap replace everything to go ahead. a manual backup and an automatic one are the same kind of file, and restore from a backup opens both. restoring works from any encrypted backup file. let damla back up on its own automatic backups write the same kind of encrypted file to a folder you pick, at most once a day. open settings, then backup and your data , then automatic backup . tap choose a folder and start and pick a folder in the files picker. type a passphrase of at least 8 characters and tap start . damla writes the first file at once. from then on, an encrypted copy is saved to that folder once a day, when you leave the app. note: the automatic backup keeps its passphrase in this phone's keychain, so you do not have to type it again. you still need it to restore, so keep a copy of it somewhere outside the phone as well. turning it off with stop automatic backups does not delete the files already written. good to know limit: an automatic backup runs only when you leave the app. if you do not open damla for several days, nothing is backed up in that time. a backup you export by hand gets a name that starts with damla- , then today's date, ending in .damlabackup . an automatic backup's file name starts with damla-auto- , then the date, ending in .damlabackup . today's file replaces the earlier one for the same day. a folder in icloud drive keeps the automatic backup off this phone too. on the automatic backup screen you can see the folder and when the last backup ran, and tap back up now to run one straight away. the newest 7 automatic backups are kept; older ones are removed automatically. if the last automatic backup is at least three days old, damla shows a reminder on today. if you have never set up an automatic backup and have been recording for a while, today shows a "back up your data" row instead. if a trial or subscription has ended, damla becomes read-only, but exporting and restoring a backup still work. if the passphrase of an existing backup is lost, the file cannot be opened. check that you still remember it before you rely on the file. related settings, page by page export and the family snapshot privacy and your data troubleshooting

title: Export and the family snapshot
summary: A spreadsheet of your transactions, and a read-only picture for family.
text: two ways to hand your numbers to others: a spreadsheet of every transaction, and a read-only picture of today's numbers for a family member. both files are made on the phone — no server is involved — and you pass them on yourself. when to use it you want your transactions in a spreadsheet, for your own sorting or for an accountant. someone in your household — a partner, a grown-up child — wants to see where the money stands, without running the books. you are moving out of the app and want a copy of the raw data (for a complete copy, encrypted, see backup and restore ). everything is in settings. open today, tap the gear at the top right, then backup and your data . step by step export your transactions as a spreadsheet open settings, then backup and your data . in the backup section, find export transactions . choose all , or a single year. tap make a csv file . when it says the file is ready, tap the share button that appears. save the file to files, or send it to your mac. the file is ordinary csv with one row per transaction, oldest first. each row has the date, the type ( spent , received , transfer , adjustment or opening balance ), the payee, the category and the account. it also has a second account column for transfers, the amount with its currency, any note, and where the record came from. money spent is negative and money received positive. a transfer between your own accounts shows both accounts and is not counted as spending. tip: pick a single year if you only need part of the history. choose all to get everything. make a snapshot for family open settings, then backup and your data , then the family section. tap make a snapshot for family . type a passphrase of at least 6 characters and tap create . you will give this phrase to the person who opens the file. when the snapshot is ready, use the share button to send the file to them — messages, mail, airdrop, whatever you already use. how they open it they open the file on a phone that has damla installed. on the first welcome screen they tap open a family snapshot ; once a snapshot is already open, the button is called open a newer snapshot . they pick the file, type the passphrase you told them, and tap open . what they see is a read-only screen titled family view . a note on it says when the picture was made and which day it is a picture of ("as of …"). on the screen: safe to spend , with a headline such as the day of the next income, or a warning that money may run short. balance today, lowest point ahead , and minimum kept . a small chart under next 90 days , showing the balance over the coming days. next to leave : the payments coming up. accounts : each account with its balance (a card shows what is owed on it). they can open a newer snapshot when you send one, and tap stop viewing to close it. good to know the snapshot is a picture of one moment. it does not update by itself; send a fresh one when the numbers change. it is encrypted with the passphrase, and it is read-only: the other person can look but cannot change anything, and their phone does not receive your books. the snapshot is much smaller than a backup: it holds today's numbers and the 90-day picture, not your whole history and not your backups. passphrase lengths differ: at least 6 characters for a snapshot, at least 8 for an encrypted backup. note: exporting a csv, and making and opening snapshots, work even when a trial or subscription has ended, because they are read-only actions. related backup and restore settings, page by page privacy and your data

title: Privacy and your data
summary: What stays on the phone, what is looked up online, and what is never sent.
text: your books stay on your phone. the reading of your words happens on the phone. the few things that go online carry nothing about you. this page says what stays, what goes, and what never leaves. when to read this you want to know where your balances and transactions are stored before you trust the app with them. you want to know what, if anything, is sent over the internet. you are setting damla up for someone who cares about privacy, and want the short version. what stays on the phone your accounts, balances, transactions, notes and plans are stored only on this phone. there is no server they sit on. there is no account, no sign-in, no server, no advertising and no analytics. damla declares to apple that it does not track anyone, and lists no tracking domains. when you back up, the file is encrypted with a passphrase only you know, and you choose where it is saved — a folder in icloud drive, if you like, or anywhere else in files. passwords damla keeps for locked statement pdfs stay in this phone's keychain. they never leave the phone and are not in backups. reminders about bills and about your balance dipping below your minimum are worked out on this phone, from your own data. a bank alert that arrives while the phone is locked waits on the phone and is added the next time you open and unlock the app. the lock damla locks with face id, or your passcode, when you leave it. in settings under basics , ask for face id , you choose how soon it asks again: every time, or after 1, 5 or 15 minutes away. the automations you set up in the shortcuts app do not need the lock. reading your words, on the phone damla understands plain sentences — "school fees on the card, later paid in instalments" — so you do not have to fill in forms. the understanding is done by the language model built into your iphone where it supports apple intelligence, and by a simple reader built into damla where it does not. in both cases the work runs on the phone: nothing you type is sent anywhere. the maths — balances, forecasts, instalments — is done by ordinary code, and that never leaves the phone either. what is looked up online, and what it sends three look-ups exist. none is required, and the app works fully offline. exchange-rate refresh is on by default and you can switch it off; the price lookup and the logo search happen only if you turn them on or tap them. the app's privacy declaration to apple lists these three as the only data that ever leaves the phone. look-up what it sends when exchange rates currency codes only, for example "aed", "usd" about once a day, if you leave update exchange rates daily on, or when you tap refresh now prices for holdings the ticker symbols of holdings you choose to track, for example "aapl" only if you turn on look up prices for holdings — it is off by default find logo online the bank name you typed only when you tap the button, for a bank missing from the built-in catalog the rates and prices come back with an as-of date, and the last one is shown in settings under currencies and prices , so you can always see where each number came from. you can also type your own rate or price, and a value you type wins on the day you enter it. note: no amounts, account names, dates, notes or personal details are ever part of a look-up. damla never connects to your bank, and nothing carries an account, device or advertising identifier, or is linked to you. what is never sent anywhere balances and transactions. anything you type: sentences, notes, and the questions you ask damla. bank messages and statement files. ios gives apps no access to your messages; they reach damla only through a shortcut you set up, the share sheet or the file picker, and they are read on the phone. one-time codes that appear in messages. the code is never kept — it reaches neither the books nor the inbox — and the log of recent alerts records only that a code was skipped, never the message. the content of a family snapshot shared with someone: the file is encrypted with a passphrase, and you pass it on yourself. taking your data out you are not locked in. in settings, backup and your data , you can export a csv spreadsheet of all transactions, make an encrypted backup sealed with a passphrase that only you know, and make a read-only snapshot for family. and delete all data erases everything on this phone at once. careful: damla shows estimates from the numbers you give it. it gives information, not financial, tax or investment advice. related backup and restore export and the family snapshot prices and exchange rates logos and account details

title: Troubleshooting
summary: When a number looks wrong or an alert does not arrive.
text: this page covers two kinds of problem: a bank message that never reached damla, and a figure in your books that needs a correction. the checks below show which one you have. each fix touches one record. when to use it a bank message was not added as a transaction, or you do not know where it went. an account's balance differs from what your bank shows. a holding's value or cost looks wrong, or a staged purchase payment has the wrong amount. the safe-to-spend number looks too high or too low, or a rate or price did not change after a refresh. step by step when a bank message did not arrive: open settings, tap bank messages and statements , then automations (shortcuts) , and look at the is it working? section. it shows when the last bank message reached damla, or says nothing has reached damla yet . it also tells you if statements are waiting for your review , and has a button to open the shortcuts app . send yourself a test message, as the note under that section suggests. tap recent alerts . a test message should appear there within a minute. if it does not, the automation is not running. look at the reason shown next to the entry. if the message is listed but was not added, the reason is written there. for example, the card's last digits are not known yet: enter them once in the inbox and damla learns them. if nothing is listed at all, open your automation in the shortcuts app and check that it is set to run immediately , and that the trigger matches your bank's messages (the sender or keyword you chose). check the action itself too: its text field must hold shortcut input , the blue pill suggestion above the keyboard, not words you typed yourself. tip: while testing, you can leave notify when run switched on in the automation; the steps on the automations screen tell you to switch it off if you see it. tip: if one of damla's actions is missing when you tap add action in shortcuts, open damla, force-quit shortcuts and open it again. if it is still missing, restart the iphone. the automations screen lists the four actions to look for under damla's actions . good to know a balance is different from the bank correct the account to the balance your bank shows. damla adds one adjustment that is not income or spending, so the correction is recorded without turning into earnings or costs. a holding's value or cost is wrong open the holding. tap what it cost to correct what you paid for it. under values on file , tap a wrong value to correct it, or swipe it away to delete it. the newest value is the one in force, and a value you type on a day beats a fetched one from the same day. a staged payment has the wrong amount open the purchase and tap the payment to change its amount or date, or swipe the payment to delete it. the rate or price did not change after a refresh tap refresh now in settings and read the report: it says for each source whether it was updated , skipped (with the reason, such as price lookup being off or no tickers set) or failed (with the error). a rate or price you typed today is used until the next refresh replaces it. the safe-to-spend number looks too high or low open the forecast from your balance ahead on today and look at the lowest point. then check that your income and bills are in plan, income & bills, that each card has a billing cycle and a paying account, and that the look ahead setting is what you want: it sets how far ahead safe to spend looks, at least. note: if something is still unclear after all this, it is probably a gap in the app, not a mistake of yours. note what you did and what you expected to happen. related how automatic capture works what damla ignores, and undoing an alert the inbox forecast and safe to spend
